gratified. Listen to me, O king of kings, as I tell thee this, O sinless
one. There is complete happiness in abstaining from meat, O monarch. He
that undergoes severe austerities for a hundred years and he that
abstains from meat, are both equal in point of merit. Even this is my
opinion, In the lighted fortnight of the month of Karttika in especial,
one should abstain from honey and meat. In this, it has been ordained,
there is great merit. He who abstains from meat for the four months of
the rains acquires the four valued blessings of achievements, longevity,
fame and might. He who abstains for the whole month of Karttika from meat

  "passage_text": "SECTION CXVII

"'Yudhishthira said, "Desiring to die or desiring to live, many persons
give up their lives in the great sacrifice (of battle). Tell me, O
grandsire, what is the end that these attain to. To throw away life in
battle is fraught with sorrow for men. O thou of great wisdom, thou
knowest that to give up life is difficult for men whether they are in
prosperity, or adversity, in felicity or calamity. In my opinion, thou
art possessed of omniscience. Do thou tell me the reason of this."

"'Bhishma said, "In prosperity or adversity, in happiness or woe, living
creatures, O lord of the earth, coming into this world, live according to
a particular tenor. Listen to me as I explain the reason to thee. The
question thou hast asked me is excellent, O Yudhishthira! In this
connection, O king, I shall explain to thee the old narrative of the
discourse that took place in former times between the Island-born Rishi
and a crawling worm. In days of old, when that learned Brahmana, viz.,
the Island-born Krishna, having identified himself with Brahma, roamed
over the world, he beheld, on a road over which cars used to pass, a worm
moving speedily. The Rishi was conversant with the course of every
creature and the language of every animal. Possessed of omniscience, he
addressed the worm he saw in these words.

"'"Vyasa said, 'O worm, thou seemest to be exceedingly alarmed, and to be
in great haste. Tell me, whither dost thou run, and whence hast thou been
afraid.'

"'"The worm said, 'Hearing the rattle of yonder large car I am filled with
fear. O thou of great intelligence, fierce is the roar it makes. It is
almost come! The sound is heard. Will it not kill me? It is for this that
I am flying away. The sound, as it is heard from a near point, I catch,
of the bulls I hear. They are breathing hard under the whip of the
driver, as they are drawing the heavy burden. I hear also the diverse
sounds made by the men who are driving the bulls. Such sounds are
incapable of being heard by a creature that like us has taken his birth
in the order of worms. It is for this reason that I am flying from this
situation of great fright. Death is felt by all creatures to be fraught
with pain. Life is an acquisition difficult to make. Hence, I fly away in
fear, I do not wish to pass from a state of happiness to one of woe.'"

"'Bhishma continued, "Thus addressed, the Island-born Vyasa said, 'O worm,
whence can be thy happiness? Thou belongest to the intermediate order of
being. I think, death would be fraught with happiness to thee! Sound,
touch, taste, scent, and diverse kinds of excellent enjoyments are
unknown to thee, O worm! I think, death will prove a benefit to thee!'

"'"The worm said, 'A living creature, in whatever situation he may be
placed, becomes attached to it. In even this order of being I am happy, I
think, O thou of great wisdom! It is for this that I wish to live. In
even this condition, every object of enjoyment exists for me according to
the needs of my body. Human beings and those creatures that spring from
immobile objects have different enjoyments. In my former life I was a
human being. O puissant one, I was a Sudra possessed of great wealth. I
was not devoted to the Brahmanas. I was cruel, vile in conduct, and a
usurer. I was harsh in speech. I regarded cunning as wisdom. I hated all
creatures. Taking advantage of pretexts in compacts made between myself
and others, I was always given to taking away what belonged to others.
Without feeding servants and guests arrived at my house, I used to fill,
when hungry, my own stomach, under the impulse of pride, covetous of good
food. Greedy I was of wealth, I never dedicated, with faith and
reverence, any food to the deities and the Pitris although duty required
me to dedicate food unto them. Those men that came to me, moved by fear,
for seeking my protection, I sent adrift without giving them any
protection. I did not extend my protection to those that came to me with
prayers for dispelling their fear. I used to feel unreasonable envy at
seeing other people's wealth, and corn, and spouses held dear by them,
and articles of drink, and good mansions. Beholding the happiness of
others, I was filled with envy and I always wished them poverty.
Following that course of conduct which promised to crown my own wishes
with fruition, I sought to destroy the virtue, wealth, and pleasures of
other people. In that past life of mine, I committed diverse deeds
largely fraught with cruelty and such other passions. Recollecting those
acts I am filled with repentance and grief even as one is filled with
grief at the loss of one's dear son. In consequence of these acts of mine
I do not know what the fruits are of good deeds. I, however, worshipped
my old mother and on one occasion worshipped a Brahmana. Endued with
birth and accomplishments, that Brahmana, in course of his wanderings,
came to my house once as a guest. I received him with reverent
hospitality. In consequence of the merit attaching to that act, my memory
has not forsaken me. I think that in consequence of that act I shall once
more succeed in regaining happiness. O thou of ascetic wealth, thou
knowest everything. Do thou in kindness tell me what is for my good.'"'""
}

  "passage_text": "SECTION CXVIII\n\n\"'\"Vyasa said, 'It is in consequence of a meritorious act, O worm, that\nthou, though born in the intermediate order of being, art not stupefied.\nThat act is mine, O worm, in consequence of which thou art not\nstupefied.[527] In consequence of the puissance of my penances, I am able\nto rescue a being of demerit by granting him a sight only of my person.\nThere is no stronger might than the might that attaches to penances. I\nknow, O worm, that thou hast taken birth in the order of worms through\nthe evil acts of thy past life. If, however, thou thinkest of attaining\nto righteousness and merit, thou mayst again attain to it. Deities as\nwell as beings crowned with ascetic success, enjoy or endure the\nconsequence of acts done by them in this field of action. Amongst men\nalso, when acts of merit are performed, they are performed from desire of\nfruit (and not with disregard for fruit). The very accomplishment that\none seeks to acquire are sought from desire of the happiness they will\nbring.[528] Learned or ignorant (in a former life) the creature that is,\nin this life, destitute of speech and understanding and hands and feet,\nis really destitute of everything.[529] He that becomes a superior\nBrahmana adores, while alive, the deities of the sun and the moon,\nuttering diverse sacred Mantras. O worm, thou shalt attain to that state\nof existence. Attaining to that status, thou wilt enjoy all the elements\nconverted into articles of enjoyment. When thou hast attained to that\nstate, I shall impart to thee Brahma. Or, if thou wishest, I may place\nthee in any other status!' The worm, agreeing to the words of Vyasa, did\nnot leave the road, but remained on it. Meanwhile, the large vehicle\nwhich was coming in that direction came to that spot.[530] Torn to pieces\nby the assault of the wheels, the worm gave up his life-breath. Born at\nlast in the Kshatriya order through the grace of Vyasa of immeasurable\npuissance, he proceeded to see the great Rishi. He had, before becoming a\nKshatriya, to pass through diverse orders of being, such as hedgehog and\nIguana and boar and deer and bird, and Chandala and Sudra and Vaisya.\nHaving given an account of his various transformations unto the\ntruth-telling Rishi, and remembering the Rishi's kindness for him, the\nworm (now transformed into a Kshatriya) with joined palms fell at the\nRishi's feet and touched them with his head.\n\n\"'\"The worm said, 'My present status is that high one which is coveted by\nall and which is attainable by the possession of the ten well-known\nattributes. Indeed, I who was formerly a worm have thus attained to the\nstatus of a prince. Elephants of great strength, decked with golden\nchains, bear me on their backs. Unto my cars are yoked Kamvoja steeds of\nhigh mettle. Numerous vehicles, unto which are attached camels and mules,\nbear me. With all my relatives and friends I now eat food rich with meat.\nWorshipped by all, I sleep, O highly blessed one, on costly beds in\ndelightful rooms into which disagreeable winds cannot blow. Towards the\nsmall hours of every night, Sutas and Magadhas and encomiasts utter my\npraises even as the deities utter the agreeable praises of Indra, their\nchief. Through the grace of thyself that art firm in truth and endued\nwith immeasurable energy, I who was before a worm have now become a\nperson of the royal order. I bow my head to thee, O thou of great wisdom.\nDo thou command me as to what I should do now. Ordained by the puissance\nof thy penances, even this happy status hath now become mine!'\n\n\"'\"Vyasa said, 'I have today been worshipped by thee, O king, with diverse\nwords expressive of reverence. Transformed into a worm, thy memory had\nbecome clouded. That memory has again appeared. The sin thou committed in\na former life has not yet been destroyed,--that sin, viz., which was\nearned by thee while thou wert a Sudra covetous of wealth and cruel in\nbehaviour and hostile to the Brahmanas. Thou wert able to obtain a sight\nof my person. That was an act of merit to thee while thou wert a worm. In\nconsequence of thy having saluted and worshipped me thou shalt rise\nhigher, for, from the Kshatriya order thou shalt rise to the status of a\nBrahmana, if only thou castest off thy life-breaths on the field of\nbattle for the sake of kine or Brahmanas. O prince, enjoying much\nfelicity and performing many sacrifices with copious presents, thou shalt\nattain to heaven and transformed into eternal Brahma, thou wilt have\nperfect beatitude. Those that take birth in the intermediate order (of\nanimals) become (when they rise) Sudras. The Sudra rises to the status of\nthe Vaisya; and the Vaisya to that of the Kshatriya. The Kshatriya who\ntakes pride in the discharge of the duties of his order, succeeds in\nattaining to the status of a Brahmana. The Brahmana, by following a\nrighteous conduct, attains to heaven that is fraught with great\nfelicity.'\"'\""

Once on a\ntime, the Island-born Krishna, O king, while wandering over the world in\ndisguise, proceeded to Baranasi and waited upon Maitreya who belonged by\nbirth to a race of Munis[531]. Seeing Vyasa arrive, that foremost of\nRishis, viz., Maitreya, gave him a seat and after worshipping him with\ndue rites, fed him with excellent food. Having eaten that good food which\nwas very wholesome and which produced every kind of gratification, the\nhigh-souled Krishna became exceedingly delighted and as he sat there, he\neven laughed aloud. Seeing Krishna laugh, Maitreya addressed him, saying,\n'Tell me, O righteous-souled one, what the reason is of thy laughter!\nThou art an ascetic, endued with capacity to control thy emotions. Great\njoy, it seems, has come over thee! Saluting thee, and worshipping thee\nwith bent head, I ask thee this, viz., what the puissance is of my\npenances and what the high blessedness is that is thine! The acts I do\nare different from those which thou doest. Thou art already emancipated\nthough still owning life-breaths. I, however, am not yet freed. For all\nthat I think that there is not much difference between thee and me. I am\nagain, distinguished by birth.'[532]\n\n\"'\"Vyasa said, 'This wonder that has filled me hath arisen from an\nordinance that looks like a hyperbole, and from its paradoxical statement\nfor the comprehension of the people. One\nshould never injure; one should always tell the truth; and one should\nmake gifts. The Rishis of old announced this, following the declarations\nof the Vedas. Unto a\nthirsty man thou hast given a little water with a sincere heart. Thyself\nthirsty and hungry, thou hast, by giving me such food, conquered many\nhigh regions of felicity, O puissant one, as, one does by many\nsacrifices. The fragrance of Righteousness is about thee. I\nthink that all thy acts are performed agreeably to the ordinance. O son,\nsuperior to ablutions in sacred waters, superior to the accomplishment of\nall Vedic vows, is gift. Indeed, O Brahmana, gift is more auspicious than\nall sacred acts. All those rites laid down\nin the Vedas which thou applaudest do not come up to gift, for gift\nwithout doubt, is as I hold, fraught with very superior merit. The track\nthat has been made by those men who make gifts is the track that is\ntrodden by the wise. They who make gifts are regarded as givers of even\nthe life-breaths. The duties that constitute Righteousness are\nestablished in them. As the Vedas when well-studied, as the restraining\nof the senses, as a life of universal Renunciation, even so is gift which\nis fraught with very superior merit. Thou, O son, wilt rise from joy to\ngreater joy in consequence of thy having betaken thyself to the duty of\nmaking gifts. The man of intelligence (who practises this duty) certainly\nrises from joy to greater joy. We have without doubt, met with many\ndirect instances of this. Men endued with prosperity succeed in acquiring\nwealth, making gifts, performing sacrifices, and earning happiness as the\nresult thereof. It is always observed, O thou of great wisdom, to happen\nnaturally that happiness is followed by misery and misery is followed by\nhappiness.[534] Men of wisdom have said that human beings in this world\nhave three kinds of conduct. Some are righteous, some are sinful, and\nsome are neither righteous nor sinful. The conduct of the person who is\ndevoted to Brahma is not regarded either way. His sins are never regarded\nas sins. In it is contained the\nritual in respect of the Sraddha in which have been declared the\nmysteries connected with the Pitris. The mysteries connected with all the\ndeities have also been explained there. It comprehends the duties and\npractices, productive of great merit, of the Rishis also, together with\nthe mysteries attaching to them. It contains an exposition of the merits\nof great sacrifices and those that attach to all kinds of gifts. Those\nmen who always read the scriptures bearing on these topics, those who\nbear them properly in their mind, and he who, having listened to them,\nfollows them in practice, are all regarded to be as holy and sinless as\nthe puissant Narayana himself. The merits that attach to the gift of\nkine, those that belong to the performance of ablutions in sacred waters,\nthose that are won by the performance of sacrifices,--all these are\nacquired by that man who treats guests with reverence. They who listen to\nthese scriptures, they who are endued with faith, and they who have a\npure heart, it is well-known, conquer many regions of happiness. Those\nrighteous men who are endued with faith, become cleansed of all stains\nand no sin can touch them. Such men always increase in righteousness and\nsucceed in attaining to heaven. Once on a time, a celestial messenger,\ncoming to the court of Indra of his own accord, but remaining invisible,\naddressed the chief of the deities in these words, 'At the command of\nthose two deities who are the foremost of all physicians, and who are\nendued with every desirable attribute, I have come to this place where I\nbehold human beings and Pitris and the deities assembled together. Why,\nindeed, is sexual congress interdicted for the man who performs a Sraddha\nand for him also who eats at a Sraddha (for the particular day)? Why are\nthree rice-balls offered separately at a Sraddha? Unto whom should the\nfirst of those balls be offered? Unto whom should the second one be\noffered? And whose has it been said is the third or remaining one? I\ndesire to know all this.' After the celestial messenger had said these\nwords connected with righteousness and duty, the deities who were seated\ntowards the east, the Pitris also, applauding that ranger of the sky,\nbegan as follows."
}

  "passage_text": "\"'\"The Pitris said, 'Welcome art thou, and blessings upon thee! Do thou\nlisten, O best of all rangers of the sky! The question thou hast asked is\na high one and fraught with deep meaning. The Pitris of that man who\nindulges in sexual congress on the day he performs a Sraddha, or eats at\na Sraddha, have to lie for the period of a whole month on his vital seed.\nAs regards the classification of the rice-balls offered at a Sraddha, we\nshall explain what should be done with them one after another. The first\nrice-ball should be conceived as thrown into the waters. The second ball\nshould be given to one of the wives to eat. The third ball should be cast\ninto the blazing fire. Even this is the ordinance that has been declared\nin respect of the Sraddha. Even this is the ordinance that is followed in\npractice according to the rites of religion. The Pitris of that man who\nact according to this ordinance become gratified with him and remain\nalways cheerful. The progeny of such a man increases and inexhaustible\nwealth always remains at his command.'\n\n\"'\"The celestial messenger said, 'Thou hast explained the division of the\nrice-balls and their consignment one after another to the three (viz.,\nwater, the spouse, and the blazing fire), together with the reasons\nthereof.[541] Whom does that rice-ball which is consigned to the waters\nreach? How does it, by being so consigned, gratify the deities and how\ndoes it rescue the Pitris? The second ball is eaten by the spouse. That\nhas been laid down in ordinance. How do the Pitris of that man (whose\nspouse eats the ball) become the eaters thereof? The last ball goes into\nthe blazing fire. How does that ball succeed in finding its way to thee,\nor who is he unto whom it goes? I desire to hear this,--that is, what are\nthe ends attained by the rice-balls offered at Sraddhas when thus\ndisposed of by being cast into the water, given to the spouse, and thrown\ninto the blazing fire!'\n\n\"'\"The Pitris said, 'Great is this question which thou hast asked. It\ninvolves a mystery and is fraught with wonder. We have been exceedingly\ngratified with thee, O ranger of the sky! The very deities and the Munis\napplaud acts done in honour of the Pitris. Even they do not know what the\ncertain conclusions are of the ordinances in respect of the acts done in\nhonour of the Pitris. Excepting the high souled, immortal, and excellent\nMarkandeya, that learned Brahmana of great fame, who is ever devoted to\nthe Pitris, none amongst them is conversant with the mysteries of the\nordinances in respect of the Pitris. Having heard from the holy Vyasa\nwhat the end is of the three rice-balls offered at the Sraddha, as\nexplained by the Pitris themselves in reply to the question of the\ncelestial messenger, I shall explain the same to thee. Do thou hear, O\nmonarch, what the conclusions are with respect to the ordinances about\nthe Sraddha. Listen with rapt attention, O Bharata, to me as I explain\nwhat the end is of the three rice-balls. That rice-ball which goes into\nwater is regarded as gratifying the deity of the moon. That deity, thus\ngratified, O thou of great intelligence, gratifies in return the other\ndeities and the Pitris also with them. It has been laid down that the\nsecond rice-ball should be eaten by the spouse (of the man that performs\nthe Sraddha). The Pitris, who are ever desirous of progeny, confer\nchildren on the woman of the house. Listen now to me as I tell thee what\nbecomes of the rice-ball that is cast into the blazing fire. With that\nball the Pitris are gratified and as the result thereof they grant the\nfruition of all wishes unto the person offering it. I have thus told thee\neverything about the end of the three rice-balls offered at the Sraddha\nand consigned to the three (viz., water, the spouse, and the fire). That\nBrahmana who becomes the Ritwik at a Sraddha constitutes himself, by that\nact, the Pitri of the person performing the Sraddha. Hence, he should\nabstain that day from sexual intercourse with even his own spouse[542]. O\nbest of all rangers of the sky, the man who eats at Sraddha should bear\nhimself with purity for that day. By acting otherwise, one surely incurs\nthe faults I have indicated. It cannot be otherwise. Hence, the Brahmana\nwho is invited to a Sraddha for eating the offerings should eat them\nafter purifying himself by a bath and bear himself piously for that day\nby abstaining from every kind of injury or evil. The progeny of such a\nperson multiply and he also who feeds him reaps the same reward.'\"\n\n\"'Bhishma continued, \"After the Pitris said so, a Rishi of austere\npenances, named Vidyutprabha, whose form shone with splendour like that\nof the sun, spoke. Having heard those mysteries of religion as propounded\nby the Pitris, he addressed Sakra, saying, 'Stupefied by folly, men slay\nnumerous creatures born in the intermediate orders, such as worms and\nants and snakes and sheep and deer and birds. Heavy is the measure of sin\nthey incur by these acts. What, however, is the remedy?' When this\nquestion was asked, all the gods and Rishis endued with wealth of\npenances and the highly blessed Pitris, applauded that ascetic."
}

  "passage_text": "\"'\"Sakra said, 'Thinking in one's mind of Kurukshetra and Gaya and Ganga\nand Prabhasa and the lakes of Pushkara, one should dip one's head in\nwater. By so doing one becomes cleansed of all one's sins like Chandramas\nfreed from Rahu. One should bathe in this way for three days in\nsuccession and then fast for every day. Besides this, one should touch\n(after bathing) the back of a cow and bow one's head to her tail.'\nVidyutprabha, after this, once more addressing Vasava, said, 'I shall\ndeclare a rite that is more subtle. Listen to me, O thou of a hundred\nsacrifices. Rubbed with the astringent powder of the hanging roots of the\nbanian and anointed with the oil of Priyangu, one should eat the\nShashtika paddy mixed with milk. By so doing one becomes cleansed of all\none's sins[543]. Listen now to another mystery unknown to many but which\nwas discovered by the Rishis with the aid of meditation. I heard it from\nVrihaspati while he recited it in the presence of Mahadeva. O chief of\nthe deities, do thou hear it with Rudra in thy company, O lord of Sachi!\nIf a person, ascending a mountain, stands there on one foot, with arms\nupraised and joined together, and abstaining from food looks at a blazing\nfire, he acquires the merits of severe penances and obtains the rewards\nthat attach to fasts. Heated by the rays of the sun, he becomes cleansed\nof all his sins. One who acts in this way in both the summer and the\nwinter seasons, becomes freed from every sin. Cleansed of every sin, one\nacquires a splendour of complexion for all time. Such a man blazes with\nenergy like the Sun or shines in beauty like the Moon!' After this, the\nchief of the deities, viz., he of a hundred sacrifices, seated in the\nmidst of the gods, then sweetly addressed Vrihaspati, saying these\nexcellent words, 'O holy one, do thou duly discourse on what those\nmysteries of religion are that are fraught with happiness to human\nbeings, and what the faults are which they commit, together with the\nmysteries that attach to them!'\n\n\"'\"Vrihaspati said, 'They who pass urine, facing the sun, they who do not\nshow reverence for the wind, they who do not pour libations on the\nblazing fire, they who milk a cow whose calf is very young, moved by the\ndesire of obtaining from her as much milk as possible, commit sins. I\nshall declare what those faults are, O lord of Sachi! Do thou listen to\nme. The Sun, Wind, the bearer of sacrificial oblations, O Vasava, and\nkine who are the mothers of all creatures, were created by the Self-born\nhimself, for rescuing all the worlds, O Sakra! These are the deities of\nhuman beings. Listen all of ye to the conclusions of religion. Those\nwicked men and wicked women who pass urine facing the sun, live in great\ninfamy for six and eighty years. That man, O Sakra, who cherishes no\nreverence for the wind, gets children that fall away prematurely from the\nwomb of his spouse. Those men who do not pour libations on the blazing\nfire find that the fire, when they do ignite it for such rites as they\nwish to perform, refuses to eat their libations[544]. Those men who drink\nthe milk of kine whose calves are very young, never get children for\nperpetuating their races.[545] Such men see their children die and their\nraces shrink. Even these are the consequences of the acts referred to, as\nobserved by regenerate persons venerable for age in their respective\nraces. Hence, one should always avoid that which has been interdicted,\nand do only that which has been directed to be done, if one is desirous\nof achieving prosperity. This that I say unto thee is very true.' After\nthe celestial preceptor had said this, the highly blessed deities, with\nthe Maruts, and the highly blessed Rishis questioned the Pitris, saying,\n'Ye Pitris, at what acts of human beings, who are generally endued with\nlittle understanding, do ye become gratified? What gifts, made in course\nof such rites as are gone through for improving the position of deceased\npersons in the other world, become inexhaustible in respect of their\nefficacy?[546] By performing what acts can men become freed from the debt\nthey owe to the Pitris? We desire to hear this. Great is the curiosity we\nfeel.'\n\n\"'\"The Pitris said, 'Ye highly blessed ones, the doubt existing in your\nminds has been properly propounded. Listen as we declare what those acts\nare of righteous men that gratify us. Bulls endued with blue complexion\nshould be set free. Gifts should be made to us, on the day of the new\nmoon, of sesame seeds and water. In the season of rains, lamps should be\nlighted. By these acts of men, they can free themselves from the debt\nthey owe to the Pitris.[547] Such gifts never become vain. On the other\nhand, they become inexhaustible and productive of high fruits. The\ngratification we derive from them is regarded to be inexhaustible. Those\nmen who, endued with faith, beget offspring, rescue their deceased\nancestors from miserable Hell'. Hearing these words of the Pitris,\nVriddha-Gargya, possessed of wealth of penances and high energy, became\nfilled with wonder so that the hair on his body stood erect. Addressing\nthem he said, 'Ye that are all possessed of wealth of penances, tell us\nwhat the merits are that attach to the setting free of bulls endued with\nblue complexion. What merits, again, attach to the gift of lamps in the\nseason of rains and the gift of water with sesame seeds?'"

"'Bhishma said, "The chief of the deities, Indra, after the Pitri has
ceased to speak, addressed the puissant Hari, saying, 'O Lord, what are
those acts by which thou becomest gratified? How, indeed, do men succeed
in gratifying thee?'

"'"Vishnu said, 'That which I greatly hate is the detraction of Brahmanas;
without doubt, if the Brahmanas are worshipped, I regard myself
worshipped. All superior Brahmanas should always be saluted with
reverence, after feeding them with hospitality. One should reverence
one's own feet also (in the evening). I am gratified with men who act in
this way, as also with those who worship and make offerings to the whirl
that is noticeable on cowdung (when it first drops from the cow)[548].
They who behold a Brahmana that is a dwarf in stature, or a boar that has
just risen from water and that bears on his head a quantity of mud taken
up from the bank, have never to meet with any evil. They become freed
from every sin. That man who worships every day the Aswattha (Ficus
religiosa) and the substance called Gorochana and the cow, is regarded as
worshipping the whole universe with the deities and Asuras and human
beings. Verily, staying within these, I accept, in my own form, the
worship that is offered to them. The worship that is offered to these is
the worship offered to me. This has been so as long as the worlds have
been created. Those men of little understanding that worship me in a
different way worship me in vain, for the worship of that kind I never
accept. Verily, the worship of other kinds is not at all gratifying to
me.'

"'"Indra said, 'Why dost thou applaud the circular marks on cowdung, the
feet, the boar, the Brahmana that is a dwarf in stature, and mud raised
up from the soil? It is thou who createst and it is thou who destroyest
them. Thou art the eternal nature of all mortal or transitory things.'"

"'Bhishma continued, "Hearing these words of Indra, Vishnu smiled a little
and then said, 'It was with my circular disc that the Daityas were slain.
It was with my two feet that the world was covered. Assuming the form of
a boar I slew Hiranyaksha. Assuming the form of a dwarf I conquered (the
Asura) king Vali. Those high-souled men who worship these gratify me.
Verily, they who worship me in these forms never meet with discomfiture.
If one beholding a Brahmana leading the Brahmacharya mode of life arrived
at one's house, offers unto him the first portion of one's food that
belongs as of right to a Brahmana, and eats what remains thereafter, one
is regarded as eating Amrita. If one, after adoring the morning twilight,
stands with face directed towards the sun, one reaps the merit that
attaches to the performance of ablutions in all tirthas and becomes
cleansed of all sins. Ye Rishis possessed of wealth of penances, I have
told you in details what constitutes a great mystery. On what else shall
I discourse unto you? Tell me your doubts.'

"'"Baladeva said, 'Listen now to another great mystery that is fraught with
happiness to men. Ignorant persons, unacquainted with it, meet with much
distress at the hands of other creatures. That man who, rising at early
dawn, touches a cow, ghee, and curds, as also mustard seeds and the
larger variety thereof called Priyangu, becomes cleansed of all sins. As
regards Rishis possessed of wealth of penances, they always avoid all
creatures both before and behind, as also all that is impure while
performing Sraddhas.'[549]

"'"The deities said, 'If a person, taking a vessel of copper, filling it
with water, and facing the east, resolves upon a fast or the observance
of a particular vow, the deities become gratified with him and all his
wishes become crowned with success. By observing fasts, or vows in any
other way, men of little understandings gain nothing.[550] In uttering
the resolution about the observance of fasts and in making offerings to
the deities, the use of a vessel of copper is preferable. In presenting
the offerings to the deities, in (giving and accepting) alms, in
presenting the ingredients of the Arghya and in offering oblations of
water mixed with sesame seeds to the Pitris, a vessel of copper should be
used. By doing these acts in any other way, one acquires little merit.
Even these mysteries have been laid down relating to how the deities are
gratified.'

"'"Dharma said, 'The offerings made in all rites in honour of the deities
and in those in honour of the Pitris should never be given away to a
Brahmana that has accepted service under the king, or that rings the bell
or attends to subsidiary duties in acts of worship or at Sraddhas, or
that keeps kine, or that is engaged in trade, or that follows some art as
a profession, or that is an actor, or that quarrels with friends or that
is destitute of Vedic studies, or that marries a Sudra woman[551]. The
performer of the Sraddha who gives away such offerings unto such a
Brahmana falls away from prosperity and multiplies not his race. He
fails, again, to gratify his Pitris by doing such an act. From the house
of that person whence a guest returns unsatisfied, the Pitris, the
deities, and the sacred fires, all return disappointed in consequence of
such treatment of the guest. That man who does not discharge the duties
of hospitality towards the guest arrived at his abode, comes to be
regarded as equally sinful with those that are slayers of women or of
kine, that are ungrateful towards benefactors, that are slayers of
Brahmanas, or that are violators of the beds of their preceptors.'"

I shall recite the\ndemerits of that man of wicked understanding who lifts up his feet for\nstriking therewith a cow or a highly blessed Brahmana or a blazing fire.\nThe infamy of such a man spreads throughout the world and touches the\nconfines of heaven itself. His Pitris become filled with fear. The\ndeities also become highly dissatisfied on his account. Endued with great\nenergy, Fire refuses to accept the libations poured by him. For a hundred\nlives he has to rot in hell. He is never rescued at any time. One should,\ntherefore, never touch a cow with one's feet, or a Brahmana of high\nenergy, or a blazing fire, if one is endued with faith and desires one's\nown good. He who offers the\nPitris rice boiled in sugared milk, sitting with face directed to the\nsouth at noontide in the shade caused by an elephant's body, in the month\nof Bhadrapada, under the constellation Magha, acquires great merits.\nListen to what those merits are. Thou tookest thy\nstation in the firmament and in the path of Agni. The deities with Narada\namong them adored thee on that occasion by calling thee Sarvamsaha. Such\nman attains to the region of Purandara. He acquires, besides, the merits\nthat attach to kine, and the splendour of Chandramas also. Such a man\nbecomes freed from every sin, every fear, every grief. At the end, he\nobtains residence in the happy region of the Thousand-eyed Indra!'\"\n\n\"'Bhishma continued, \"After this, the highly blessed and celebrated seven\nRishis, with Vasishtha at their head, rose and circumambulating the\nLotus-born Brahman, stood around him with hands joined in reverence.\nVasishtha, that foremost of all persons conversant with Brahma, became\ntheir spokesman and asked this question that is beneficial to every\ncreature, but especially so to Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, 'By doing what\nacts may men of righteous conduct who are, however, destitute of the good\nof this world, succeed in acquiring merits attaching to sacrifices?'\nHearing this question of theirs, the Grandsire Brahman began to say what\nfollows.\n\n\"'\"Brahman said, 'Excellent is this question, ye highly blessed ones! It is\nat once auspicious and high and fraught with a mystery. This question\nthat ye have put is subtil and is fraught with high benefit to mankind.\nYe Rishis possessed of wealth of penances, I shall recite everything to\nyou in detail. Do ye listen with attention to what I say as to how men\nacquire the merits attaching to sacrifices (even when they are unable to\nperform them through poverty.) In the lighted fortnight of the month of\nPausha, when the constellation Rohini is in conjunction, if one,\npurifying oneself by a bath, lies under the cope of heaven, clad in a\nsingle piece of raiment, with faith and concentrated attention, and\ndrinks the rays of the moon, one acquires the merits that attach to the\nperformance of great sacrifices. Ye foremost of regenerate persons, this\nis a high mystery that I declare unto you in reply to your questions, ye\nthat are possessed of insight into the subtil truths of all topics of\nenquiry.'\"'\""

One\nof those consists of a palmful of water and the other called Akshata\nconsists of rice-grains with ghee. One should, on the day of the full\nmoon, stand facing that bright orb and make unto him the two offerings\nmentioned, viz., a palmful of water and the rice-grains with ghee called\nAkshata. The man who presents these offerings is said to adore his sacred\nfire. Verily, he is regarded as one that has poured libations on the\nthree (principal) fires. That man of little understanding who cutteth\ndown a large tree on the day of the new moon, becomes stained with the\nsin of Brahmanicide. Praise be to thee! I\ngrant thee this boon, viz., that thy penances will continually increase!'"

The\nmerits that attach to the gift of water for drink are excellent. In the\nnext world in especial, those merits are very high. For them that make\ngifts of water for drink there is ordained in the other world a large\nriver full of excellent water. Indeed, the water contained in that river\nis inexhaustible and cool and sweet as nectar. He who makes gifts of\nwater in this world drinks from that stream in the world hereafter when\nhe goes thither. Listen now to the abundant merits that attach to the\ngiving of lamps. The man who gives lamps in this world has never to even\nbehold the thick darkness (of Hell). Soma and Surya and the deity of fire\nalways give him their light when he repairs to the other world. The\ndeities ordain that on every side of such a person there should be\nblazing light. Such a man is regarded as having made a gift of\na hundred kine with a bull, a gift that is productive of eternal merit.\nThe gift of a single Kapila cow is capable of cleansing whatever sins the\ngiver may be guilty of even if those sins be as grave. Brahmanicide, for\nthe gift of a single Kapila cow is regarded as equal in point of merit to\nthat of a hundred kine. Hence, one should give away a Kapila cow at that\nPushkara which is regarded as the senior (of the two Tirthas known by\nthat name) on the day of the full moon in the month of Karttika. Men that\nsucceed in making such a gift have never to encounter distress of any\nkind, or sorrow, or thorns giving pain. That man who gives away a pair of\nsandals unto a superior Brahmana that is deserving of the gift, attains\nto similar merits. By giving away an umbrella a person obtains\ncomfortable shade in the next world. (He will not have to be exposed to\nthe sun). A gift made to a deserving person is never lost. It is certain\nto produce agreeable consequences to the giver.' Hearing these opinions\nof Chitragupta, Surya's hairs stood on their ends. Endued with great\nsplendour, he addressed all the deities and the Pitris, saying 'Ye have\nheard the mysteries relating to duty, as propounded by the high-souled\nChitragupta. Those human beings who, endued with faith, make these gifts\nunto high-souled Brahmanas, become freed from fear of every kind. These\nfive kinds of men, stained with vicious deeds, have no escape. Verily, of\nsinful behaviour and regarded as the worst of men, they should never be\ntalked to. Indeed they should always be avoided. Those five are he who is\nthe slayer of a Brahmana, he who is the slayer of a cow, he who is\naddicted to sexual congress with other people's wives, he who is bereft\nof faith (in the Vedas), and he who derives his sustenance by selling the\nvirtue of his wife. These men of sinful conduct, when they repair to the\nregion of the dead, rot in hell like worms that live upon pus and blood.\nThese five are avoided by the Pitris, the deities, the Snataka Brahmanas,\nand other regenerate persons that are devoted to the practice of\npenances.'\"'\""
}

From whom may a Kshatriya, a\nVaisya, and a Sudra take their food respectively?\"\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"A Brahmana may take his food from another Brahmana or\nfrom a Kshatriya or a Vaisya, but he must never accept food from a Sudra.\nA Kshatriya may take his food from a Brahmana, a Kshatriya or a Vaisya.\nHe must, however, eschew food given by Sudras who are addicted to evil\nways and who partake of all manner of food without any scruple. He partakes of the very\nfilth of the earth who takes his food thus from a Sudra. Verily, those\nBrahmanas that take their food from Sudras, take the dirt of the earth.\nIf one engages in the service of a Sudra, one is doomed to perdition\nthough one may duly perform all the rites of one's order. A Vaisya lives by distributing\nthe fruits of his own acts and agriculture. The breeding of kine and\ntrade are the legitimate work in which a Vaisya may engage without fear\nof censure. The man who abandons his own proper occupation and betakes\nhimself to that of a Sudra, should be considered as a Sudra and on no\naccount should any food be accepted from him. Professors of the healing\nart, mercenary soldiers, the priest who acts as warder of the house, and\npersons who devote a whole year to study without any profit, are all to\nbe considered as Sudras. He who takes food from a physician takes that which is no\nbetter than excrement; the food of a harlot is like urine; that of a\nskilled mechanic is like blood. If a Brahmana approved by the good, takes\nthe food of one who lives by his learning, he is regarded as taking the\nfood of a Sudra. All good men should forego such food. The food of a\nperson who is censured by all is said to be like a draught from a pool of\nblood. The acceptance of food from a wicked person is considered as\nreprehensible as the slaying of a Brahmana. One should not accept food if\none is slighted and not received with due honours by the giver. A\nBrahmana, who does so, is soon overtaken by disease, and his race soon\nbecomes extinct. By accepting food from the warder of a city, one\ndescends to the status of the lowest outcaste. If a Brahmana accepts food\nfrom one who is guilty of killing either a cow or a Brahmana or from one\nwho has committed adultery with his preceptor's wife or from a drunkard,\nhe helps to promote the race of Rakshasas. By accepting food from a\neunuch, or from an ungrateful person, or from one who has misappropriated\nwealth entrusted to his charge, one is born in the country of the Savaras\nsituated beyond the precincts of the middle country. But I have\ngrave doubts on one point. Do thou, O sire, enlighten me, do thou tell me\nwhat expiation a Brahmana should make (for the sin he incurs) upon\naccepting the different kinds of food, those especially offered in honour\nof the gods and the oblations made to the manes.\"\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"I shall tell thee, O prince, how high-souled Brahmanas\nmay be absolved from all sin incurred by accepting food from others. In\naccepting clarified butter, the expiation is made by pouring oblations on\nthe fire, reciting the Savitri hymn. In accepting sesamum, O\nYudhishthira, the same expiation has to be made. In accepting meat, or\nhoney, or salt, a Brahmana becomes purified by standing till the rising\nof the sun. If a Brahmana accepts gold from any one, he becomes cleansed\nof all sins by silently reciting the great Vedic prayer (Gayatri) and by\nholding a piece of iron in his hand in the presence of the public. In\naccepting money or clothes or women or gold, the purification is the same\nas before. In accepting food, or rice boiled in milk and sugar, or\nsugarcane juice, or sugar-cane, or oil, or any sacred thing, one becomes\npurified by bathing thrice in the course of the day, viz., at morn, noon\nand eve. If one accepts paddy, flowers, fruits, water, half-ripe barley,\nmilk, or curdled milk, or anything made of meal or flour, the expiation\nis made by reciting the Gayatri prayer a hundred times. In accepting\nshoes or clothes at obsequial ceremonies, the sin is destroyed by\nreciting devoutly the same hymn a hundred times. The acceptance of the\ngift of land at the time of an eclipse or during the period of impurity,\nis expiated by observing a fast during three successive nights. The\nBrahmana who partakes of oblations offered to deceased ancestors, in\ncourse of the dark fortnight, is purified by fasting for a whole day and\nnight. Without performing his ablutions a Brahmana should not say his\nevening prayers, nor betake himself to religious meditation, nor take his\nfood a second time. By so doing he is purified. For this reason, the\nSraddha of deceased ancestors has been ordained to be performed in the\nafternoon and then the Brahmana who has been invited beforehand should be\nfeasted. The Brahmana who partakes of food at the house of a dead person\non the third day after the death, is purified by bathing three times\ndaily for twelve days. After the expiration of twelve days, and going\nthrough the purification ceremonies duly, the sin is destroyed by giving\nclarified butter to Brahmanas. If a man takes any food in the house of a\ndead person, within ten days after the death, he should go through all\nthe expiations before mentioned, and should recite the Savitri hymn and\ndo the sin-destroying Ishti and Kushmanda penances. The Brahmana who\ntakes his food in the house of a dead person for three nights, becomes\npurified by performing his ablutions thrice daily for seven days, and\nthus attains all the objects of his desire, and is never troubled by\nmisfortunes. The Brahmana who takes his food in the company of Sudras is\npurged from all impurity by duly observing the ceremonies of\npurification. The Brahmana who takes his food in the company of Vaisyas\nis absolved from sin by living on alms for three successive nights. If a\nBrahmana takes his food with Kshatriyas, he should make expiation by\nbathing with his clothes on. By eating with a Sudra from off the same\nplate the Sudra loses his family respectability; the Vaisya by eating\nfrom off the same plate with a Vaisya, loses his cattle and friends. The\nKshatriya loses his prosperity, and the Brahmana his splendour and\nenergy. In such cases, expiations should be made, and propitiatory rites\nshould be observed, and oblations offered to the gods. The Savitri hymn\nshould be recited and the Revati rites and Kushmanda penances should be\nobserved with the view of destroying the sin. If any of the above four\nclasses partake of food partly eaten by a person of any other class, the\nexpiation is undoubtedly made by smearing the body with auspicious\nsubstances like Rochana, Durva grass, and turmeric.\"'\""

(Such\ngifts are regarded as made from free choice.) 'The person that solicits me\nis poor. He is, again, gratified with a little. They enhance the giver's merits and\nfame. The Lord of all creatures (Brahman himself) has said that one\nshould always make gifts according to one's power.\"'\""

It behoveth\nthee to discourse unto me, through affection, for my benefit as also for\nthat of my brothers, in the presence of Vasudeva himself and of all these\nkings.\"'\n\n\"Vaisampayana continued, 'Hearing these words of king Yudhishthira,\nBhishma, the son of the river called after Bhagiratha, filled with joy in\nconsequence of his affection for the monarch and his brothers, said what\nfollows.'[559]\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"I shall certainly recite to thee discourses that are\ndelightful, on the subject, O king, of the puissance of this Vishnu as\ndisplayed in days of yore and as I have heard (from my preceptors).\nListen to me also as I describe the puissance of that great god who has a\nbull for his device. For beholding him who had gone through the rite of initiation for\nthe observance of his great vow, there came to that place Narada and\nParvata, and the Island-born Krishna, and Dhaumya, that foremost of\nsilent reciters, and Devala, and Kasyapa, and Hastikasyapa. Thus seated, they began to converse sweetly with one another on\nsubjects connected with Religion and duty as also with many royal sages\nand deities. At that time the energy, in the form of fire, Narayana,\nrising from the fuel that consisted of the rigid observance of his vow,\nissued out of the mouth of Krishna of wonderful feats. That fire began to\nconsume those mountains with their trees and creepers and little plants,\nas also with their birds and deer and beasts of prey and reptiles. Soon\nthe summit of that mountain presented a distressing and pitiful\nappearance, Inhabited by animals of diverse kinds which began to utter\ncries of woe and pain, the summit soon became bereft of every living\ncreature. That fire of mighty flames, having consumed everything without\nleaving a remnant at last came back to Vishnu and touched his feet like a\ndocile disciple. That crusher of foes, viz., Krishna, beholding that\nmountain burnt, cast a benignant look upon it and thereby brought it back\nto its former condition. That mountain thereupon once more became adorned\nwith flowering trees and creepers, and once more echoed with the notes\nand cries of birds and deer and animals of prey and reptiles. Seeing that\nwonderful and inconceivable sight, all the ascetics became amazed. Their\nhairs stood on end and their vision was blurred with tears. That foremost\nof speakers, Narayana, beholding those Rishis thus filled with wonder,\naddressed them in these sweet and refreshing words, 'Why, indeed, has\nwonder filled the hearts of this assemblage of Rishis, these ascetics\nthat are always free from attachment of every kind, that are divested of\nthe idea of meum, and that are fully conversant with every sacred\nscience? It behoveth these Rishis possessed of wealth of penances and\nfreed from every stain to explain to me truly this doubt that has arisen\nin my mind.'\n\n\"'\"The Rishis said, 'It is thou that createst all the worlds, and it is\nthou that destroyest them again. It is thou that art Winter, it is thou\nthat art Summer, and it is thou that art the season of rains. Of all the\ncreatures, mobile and immobile, that are found on the earth, thou art the\nfather, thou art the mother, thou art the master, and thou art the\norigin! Even this, O slayer of Madhu, is a matter of wonder and doubt\nwith us. O source of all auspiciousness, it behoveth Thee to resolve to\nus that doubt, viz., the issue of fire from Thy mouth. Our fears being\ndispelled we shall then, O Hari, recite to thee what we have heard and\nseen.'"

Anything, however, that\nis recited by pious persons and that is heard from those that are good,\ndeserves to be accepted with respect and faith. Such discourses exist on\nearth for a long time and are as durable as characters engraved on rocks.\nI desire, therefore, to hear, at this meeting something dropping from the\nlips of persons that are good and that cannot fail to be productive of\ngood to men.' Why also, O illustrious\ndeity, hast thou restored the mountain to its former condition?   "passage_text": "SECTION CXLI

"'"'The blessed and holy one said, "In days of yore, a blessed woman was
created by Brahman, called Tilottama, by culling grains of beauty from
every beautiful object in the universe. One day, that lady of beautiful
face, unrivalled in the universe for beauty of form, came to me, O
goddess, for circumambulating me but really impelled by the desire of
tempting me. In whatever direction that lady of beautiful teeth turned, a
new face of mine instantly appeared (so eager did I become to see her).
All those faces of mine became agreeable to look at. Thus, in consequence
of the desire of beholding her, I became four-faced, through
Yoga-puissance. Thus, I showed my high Yoga-power in becoming four-faced.
With that face of mine which is turned towards the east, I exercise the
sovereignty of the universe. With that face of mine which is turned
towards the north, I sport with thee, O thou of faultless features! That
face of mine which is turned towards the west is agreeable and
auspicious. With it I ordain the happiness of all creatures. That face of
mine which is turned towards the south is terrible. With it I destroy all
creatures. I live as a Brahmacharin with matted locks on my head,
impelled by the desire of doing good to all creatures. The bow Pinaka is
always in my hand for accomplishing the purposes of the deities. In days
of yore, Indra, desirous of acquiring my prosperity, had hurled his
thunderbolt at me. With that weapon my throat was scorched. For this
reason I have become blue-throated."

"'"'Uma said, "When, O foremost of all creatures, there are so many
excellent vehicles endued with great beauty, why is it that thou hast
selected a bovine bull for thy vehicle?"

"'"'Maheswara said, "In the days of yore, the Grandsire Brahma created the
celestial cow Surabhi yielding abundant milk. After her creation there
sprang from her a large number of kine all of which yielded copious
quantities of milk sweet as nectar. Once on a time a quantity of froth
fell from the mouth of one of her calves on my body. I was enraged at
this and my wrath scorched all the kine which thereupon became
diversified in hue. I was then pacified by the Master of all the worlds,
viz., Brahma, conversant with all topics. It was he who gave me this bull
both as a vehicle for bearing me and as a device on my banner."

"'"'Uma said, "Thou hast many abodes in heaven, of diverse forms and
possessed of every comfort and luxury. Why, O holy one, dost thou reside
in the crematorium, abandoning all those delightful mansions? The
crematorium is full of the hair and bones (of the dead), abounds with
vulture and jackals, and is strewn with hundreds of funeral pyres. Full
of carrion and muddy with fat and blood, with entrails and bones strewn
all over it, and always echoing with the howls of jackals, it is
certainly an unclean place."

"'"'Maheswara said, "I always wander over the whole earth in search of a
sacred spot. I do not, however, see any spot that is more sacred than the
crematorium. Hence, of all abodes, the crematorium pleases my heart most,
shaded that it generally is by branches of the banian and adorned with
torn garlands of flowers. O thou of sweet smiles, the multitudes of
ghostly beings that are my companions love to reside in such spots. I do
not like, O goddess, to reside anywhere without those ghostly creatures
being by my side. Hence, the crematorium is a sacred abode to me. Indeed,
O auspicious lady, it seems to me to be the very heaven. Highly sacred
and possessed of great merit, the crematorium is much applauded by
persons desirous of having holy abodes."

"'"'Uma said, "O holy one, O lord of all creatures, O foremost of all
observers of duties and religious rites, I have a great doubt, O wielder
of Pinaka, O giver of boons. These ascetics, O puissant lord, have
undergone diverse kinds of austerities. In the world are seen ascetics
wandering everywhere under diverse forms and clad in diverse kinds of
attire. For benefiting this large assemblage of Rishis, as also myself,
do thou kindly resolve, O chastiser of all foes, this doubt of mine. What
indications has Religion or Duty been said to possess? How, indeed, do
men become unacquainted with the details of Religion or Duty to succeed
in observing them? O puissant lord, O thou that art conversant with
Religion, do thou tell me this."'

"'"Narada continued, 'When the daughter of Himavat put this question,
conclave of Rishis there present worshipped the goddess and adored her
with words adorned with Riks and with hymns fraught with deep import.

"'"'Maheswara said, "Abstention from injury, truthfulness of speech,
compassion towards all beings, tranquillity of soul, and the making of
gifts to the best of one's power, are the foremost duties of the
householder. Abstention from sexual congress with the spouses of other
men, protection of the wealth and the woman committed to one's charge,
unwillingness to appropriate what is not given to one, and avoidance of
honey and meat,--these are the five chief duties. Indeed, Religion or
Duty has many branches all of which are fraught with happiness. Even
these are the duties which these embodied creatures who regard duty as
superior should observe and practise. Even these are the sources of
merit."

"'"'Uma said, "O holy one, I wish to ask thee another question about which
I have great doubts. It behoveth thee to answer it and dispel my doubts.
What are the meritorious duties of the four several orders? What duties
appertain to the Brahmana? What to the Kshatriya? What are the
indications of those duties that appertain to the Vaisya? And what kind
of duties appertain to the Sudra?""
}

  "passage_text": ""'"'Maheswara said, "Listening to the mysteries of religion and duty,
observance of the vows indicated in the Vedas, attention to the sacred
fire, and accomplishment of the business of the preceptor, leading a
mendicant life, always bearing the sacred thread, constant recitation of
the Vedas, and rigid observance of the duties of Brahmacharya, are the
duties of the Brahmana. After the period of study is over, the Brahmana,
receiving the command of his preceptor, should leave his preceptor's
abode for returning to his father's house. Upon his return he should duly
wed a wife that is fit for him. Another duty of the Brahmana consists in
avoiding the food prepared by the Sudra. Walking along the path of
righteousness, always observing fasts and the practices of Brahmacharya,
are his other duties.[561] The householder should keep up his domestic
fire for daily worship. He should study the Vedas. He should pour
libations in honour of the Pitris and the deities. He should keep his
senses under proper control. He should eat what remains after serving
gods and guests and all his dependants. He should be abstemious in food,
truthful in speech, and pure both externally and internally. Attending to
guests is another duty of the householder, as also the keeping up of the
three sacrificial fires. The householder should also attend to the
ordinary sacrifices that go by the name of Ishti and should also dedicate
animals to the deities according to the ordinances. Indeed, the
performance of sacrifices is his highest duty as also a complete
abstention from injury to all creatures. Never to eat before serving the
deities and guests and dependants is another duty of the householder. The
food that remains after serving gods and guests and dependants is called
Vighasa. The householder should eat Vighasa. Indeed, to eat after the
members of one's family including servants and other dependants, is
regarded as one of the special duties of the regenerate householder, who
should be conversant with the Vedas. The conduct of husband and wife, in
the case of householder, should be equal. He should every day make
offerings of flowers and other articles unto those deities that preside
over domesticity. The householder should take care that his house is
every day properly rubbed (with cowdung and water). He should also
observe fasts every day. Well-cleaned and well-rubbed, his house should
also be every day fumigated with the smoke of clarified butter poured on
his sacred fire in honour of the deities and the Pitris. Even these are
the duties appertaining to the householder's mode of life as observable
by a regenerate person. Those duties really uphold the world. Verily,
those duties always and eternally flow from those righteous persons among
the Brahmanas that lead a life of domesticity. Do thou listen to me with
concentrated attention, O goddess, for I shall now tell thee what the
duties are which appertain to the Kshatriya and about which thou hast
asked me. From the beginning it has been said that the duty of the
Kshatriya is to protect all creatures. The king is the acquirer of a
fixed share of the merits earned by his subjects. By that means the king
becomes endued with righteousness. That ruler of men who rules and
protects his subjects righteously, acquires, by virtue of the protection
he offers to others, many regions of felicity in the world to come. The
other duties of a person of the kingly order consist of self-restraint
and Vedic study, the pouring of libations on the sacred fire, the making
of gifts, study, the bearing of the sacred thread, sacrifices, the
performance of religious rites, the support of servants and dependants,
and perseverance in acts that have been begun. Another duty of his is to
award punishments according to the offences committed. It is also his
duty to perform sacrifices and other religious rites according to the
ordinances laid down in the Vedas. Adherence to the practice of properly
judging the disputes of litigants before him, and a devotion to
truthfulness of speech, and interference for aiding the distressed, are
the other duties by discharging which the king acquires great glory both
here and hereafter. He should also lay down his life on the field of
battle, having displayed great prowess on behalf of kine and Brahmanas.
Such a king acquires in Heaven such regions of felicity as are capable of
being won by the performance of Horse-sacrifices. The duties of the
Vaisya always consist of the keeping of cattle and agriculture, the
pouring of libations on the sacred fire, the making of gifts, and study.
Trade, walking in the path of righteousness, hospitality, peacefulness,
self-restraint, welcoming of Brahmanas, and renouncing things (in favour
of Brahmanas), are the other eternal duties of the Vaisya. The Vaisya,
engaged in trade and walking in the path of righteousness, should never
sell sesame and perfumery and juices or liquid substances. He should
discharge the duties of hospitality towards all. He is at liberty to
pursue religion and wealth and pleasure according to his means and as
much as is judicious for him. The service of the three regenerate classes
constitutes the high duty of the Sudra. That Sudra who is truthful in
speech and who has subdued his senses is regarded as having acquired
meritorious penances. Verily, the Sudra, who having got a guest,
discharges the duties of hospitality towards him, is regarded as
acquiring the merit of high penances. That intelligent Sudra whose
conduct is righteous and who worships the deities and Brahmanas, becomes
endued with the desirable rewards of righteousness. O beautiful lady, I
have thus recited to thee what the duties are of the four orders. Indeed,
O blessed lady, I have told thee what their respective duties are. What
else dost thou wish to hear?""

are, verily, gods on earth. I shall at the outset tell thee what the
religious acts are which they should do and what the rewards are which
they win through them. That religion which has been ordained for the
Brahmanas is the foremost of all religions. For the sake of the
righteousness of the world, three religions were created by the Self-born
One. Whenever the world is created (or re-created), those religions are
created by the Grandsire. Do thou listen. These are the three eternal
religions. The religion that is propounded in the Vedas is the highest;

practices of those who are regarded as righteous. The Brahmans possessed

of the Vedas (or recitation of the scriptures) the means of his
living.[562] He should devote himself to the three well-known acts (of

transcend the three (viz., lust, wrath, and covetousness). He should be
the friend of all creatures. A person that possesses these attributes is
called a Brahmana. The lord of the universe declared these six acts for
the observance of Brahmanas. Listen to those eternal duties. The
performance of sacrifices, officiating at the sacrifices of others, the
making of gifts, the acceptance of gifts, teaching, and study, are the
six acts by accomplishing which a Brahmans wins religious merit. Verily,
the daily study of the Vedas is a duty. Sacrifice is (another) eternal
duty. The making of gifts according to the measure of his power and
agreeable to the ordinance, is, in his case, much applauded. Tranquillity
of mind is a high duty that has always been current among them that are
righteous. Householders of pure mind are capable of earning very great
merit. Indeed, he who cleanses his soul by the performance of the five
sacrifices, who is truthful in speech, who is free from malice, who makes

abode, and who eats the food that remains after the requirements have
been gratified of all the members of his family and dependants, wins

feet and hands, who presents the Arghya for honouring the recipient, who
duly gives seats, and beds, and lamps for lighting the darkness, and
shelter to those that come to his abode, is regarded as highly righteous.

serves food to his guests, and having honoured them duly dismisses them

divided into three portions, keeping the requirements of righteousness in
view. With one of those portions he should accomplish all acts of
righteousness. With another he should seek to gratify his cravings for
pleasure. The third portion he should lay out for increasing. The

re-birth by absorption into Brahman). I shall tell thee the conduct that
constitutes it. Listen to me in detail, O goddess. One of the duties
inculcated by that religion is compassion towards all creatures. The man
that follows it should not reside in one place for more than one day.
Desirous of achieving emancipation, the followers of this Religion free
themselves from the bonds of hope (or desire). They have no attachment to
habitation, to the Kamandalu they bear for keeping water, to the robes
that cover their loins, or the seat whereupon they rest, or the triple
stick they bear in their hands, or the bed they sleep on, or the fire
they want, or the chamber that houses them. A follower of this Religion
sets his heart upon the workings of his soul. His mind is devoted to
Supreme Brahman. He is filled with the idea of attaining to Brahman. He
is always devoted to Yoga and the Sankhya Philosophy. He desires no other
shelter than the foot of a tree. He houses himself in empty abodes of
men. He sleeps on the banks of rivers. He takes pleasure in staying by
such banks. He is freed from every attachment, and from every tie of
affection. He merges the existence of his own soul into the Supreme Soul.

Performing ablutions three times\na day is the duty of the classes, while the Homa, with water and fruits\nfrom the wilderness, belongs to the wedded recluses as performed by the\nRishis in general. Kshatriya, the Vaisya, and the Sudra, all become so through original

Brahmana, after having attained to the status of the first order, should
always protect it (by his acts). If one, who is a Kshatriya or Vaisya,
lives in the practice of those duties that are assigned to the Brahmana,
after the manner of a Brahmana he becomes (in his next life) a Brahmana.

assigned for the Kshatriya, is regarded as one that has fallen away from
the status of a Brahmana and that has become a Kshatriya. That Brahmana
of little understanding, who, impelled by cupidity and folly, follows the
practices assigned to Vaisyas forgetful of his status as a Brahmana that
is exceedingly difficult to attain, comes to be regarded as one that has
become a Vaisya. Similarly, one that is a Vaisya by birth may, by
following the practices of a Sudra, become a Sudra. Indeed, a Brahmana,
falling away from the duties of his own order, may descend to the status
of even a Sudra. Such a Brahmana, falling away from the order of his
birth and turned out of it, without attaining to the region of Brahmana
(which is his goal if he duly observes his own duties), sinks into Hell
and in his next birth becomes born as a Sudra. A highly blessed Kshatriya
or a Vaisya, that abandons those practices of his that are consistent
with the duties laid down for his order, and follows the practices laid
down for the Sudra, falls away from his own order and becomes a person of
mixed caste. It is in this way that a Brahmana, or a Kshatriya, or a
Vaisya, sinks into the status of a Sudra. That man who has attained to
clearness of vision through practice of the duties of his own order, who
is endued with knowledge and science, who is pure (in body and mind), who
is conversant with every duty and devoted to the practice of all his
duties, is sure to enjoy the rewards of righteousness. I shall now recite
to thee, O goddess, a saying uttered by Brahma (the Self-born) on this
subject. Those that are righteous and desirous of acquiring merit always
pursue with firmness the culture of the soul. The food that comes from
cruel and fierce persons is censurable. So also is the food that has been
cooked for serving a large number of persons. The same is said of the
food that is cooked in view of the first Sraddha of a deceased person. So
also is the food that is stained in consequence of the usual faults and

authority enunciated by the Grandsire with his own mouth. If a Brahmana,
who has set up the sacred fire and who performs sacrifices, were to die
with any portion of a Sudra's food remaining undigested in his stomach,
he is sure to take birth in his next life as a Sudra. In consequence of
those remains of a Sudra's food in his stomach, he falls away from the

auspicious status of a Brahmana which is so difficult to acquire,

the lusts of other people or who sells the Soma plant, or who serves a
person of an order below his, falls away from his status of
Brahmanahood.[572] That Brahmana who violates the bed of his preceptor,
or who cherishes malice towards him, or who takes pleasure in speaking
ill of him, falls away from the status of Brahmanahood even if he be
conversant with Brahman. By these good acts, again, O goddess, when

according to the ordinance. He should always wait, with obedience and
humility, upon person of the three other orders and serve them with care.

SECTION CXLIV

"'"'Uma said, "O holy one, O Lord of all beings, O thou that art worshipped
by the deities and Asuras equally, tell me what are the duties and
derelictions of men. Indeed, O puissant one, resolve my doubts. It is by
these three, viz., thought, word, and deed, that men become bound with
bonds. It is by these same three that they become freed from those bonds.
By pursuing what conduct, O god,--indeed, by what kind of acts,--by what
behaviour and attributes and words, do men succeed in ascending to
heaven?"

"'"'The god of gods said, "O goddess, thou art well-conversant with the
true import of duties. Thou art ever devoted to righteousness and
self-restraint. The question thou hast asked me is fraught with the
benefit of all creatures. It enhances the intelligence of all persons. Do
thou, therefore, listen to the answer. Those persons that are devoted to
the religion of Truth, that are righteous and destitute of the
indications of the several modes of life, and that enjoy the wealth
earned by righteous means, succeed in ascending to heaven. Those men that
are freed from all doubts, that are possessed of omniscience, and that
have eyes to behold all things, are never enchained by either virtue or
sin. Those men that are freed from all attachments can never be bound by
the chains of action. They who never injure others in thought, word, or
deed, and who never attach themselves to anything, can never be bound by
acts. They who abstain from taking the lives of any creature, who are
pious in conduct, who have compassion, who regard friends and foes in an
equal light and who are self-restrained, can never be bound by acts.
Those men that are endued with compassion towards all beings, that
succeed in inspiring the confidence of all living creatures, and that
have cast off malice in their behaviour, succeed in ascending to heaven.
Those men that have no desire to appropriate what belongs to others, that
keep themselves aloof from the wedded wives of others, and that enjoy
only such wealth as has been earned by righteous means, succeed in
ascending to heaven. Those men who behave towards the wives of other
people as towards their own mothers and sisters and daughters, succeed in
attaining to heaven. Those men that abstain from appropriating what
belongs to others, that are perfectly contented with what they possess,
and that live depending upon their own destiny, succeed in ascending to
heaven. Those men that, in their conduct, always shut their eyes against
association with other people's spouses, that are masters of their
senses, and that are devoted to righteous conduct, succeed in ascending
to heaven. Even this is the path, created by the gods, that the righteous
should follow. This is the path, freed from passion and aversion, laid
down for the righteous to follow. Those men who are devoted to their own
spouses and who seek them only in their seasons, and who turn themselves
away from indulgence in sexual pleasure, succeed in ascending to Heaven.
Conduct marked by charity and penances, and characterised by
righteousness of deeds and purity of both body and heart, should be
followed by those that are wise for the sake of adding to their merit or
for earning their means of subsistence. Those who wish to ascend to
Heaven should follow in this track and not in any other."

"'"'Uma said, "Tell me, O illustrious deity, O sinless lord of all
creatures, what are those words by which one becomes enchained and what
are those words by uttering which one may be freed from one's bonds."

"'"'Maheswara said, "Those men who never tell lies for either themselves or
for others, or in jest or for exciting laughter, succeed in ascending to
Heaven. They who never tell lies for earning their subsistence or for
earning merit or through mere caprice, succeed in ascending to Heaven.
They who utter words that are smooth and sweet and faultless, and who
welcome all whom they meet with sincerity, succeed in ascending to
Heaven. They who never utter words that are harsh and bitter and cruel,
and who are free from deceitfulness and evil of every kind, succeed in
ascending to Heaven. Those men who never utter words that are fraught
with deceit or that cause breach of understanding between friends, and
who always speak what is true and what promotes good feelings, succeed in
ascending to Heaven. Those men who avoid harsh speeches and abstain from
quarrels with others, who are impartial in their behaviour to all
creatures, and who have subjugated their souls, succeed in ascending to
Heaven. They who abstain from evil speech or sinful conversation, who
avoid such speeches as are disagreeable, and who utter only such words as
are auspicious and agreeable, succeed in ascending to Heaven. They who
never utter, under anger, such words as tear the hearts of other people,
and who, even when under the influence of wrath, speak words that are
peaceful and agreeable, succeed in ascending to Heaven. The religion, O
goddess, appertaining to speech, should always be followed by men. It is
auspicious and characterised by truth. They that are possessed of wisdom
should always avoid untruth."

"'"'Uma said, "Do thou tell me, O god of gods, O wielder of Pinaka, O thou
that art highly blessed, what those mental acts or thoughts are by which
a person may be enchained.""
}

adherence to truth, and that are contented with what belongs to them,

that bear friendly hearts towards all beings, and that entertain
compassion towards all, succeed in ascending to Heaven. Those men that
are endued with faith, that have compassion, that are holy, that seek the
company of holy men, and that are conversant with the distinctions
between right and wrong, succeed in ascending to Heaven. Those men, O
goddess, that are conversant with what the consequences are of good and
bad deeds, succeed in ascending to Heaven. Those men that are just in all
their dealings, that are endued with all desirable accomplishments, that
are devoted to the deities and the Brahmanas, and that are endued with
perseverance in the doing of good acts, succeed in ascending to Heaven.

meritorious consequences of their deeds. What else dost thou wish to
hear?"

excruciating misery. One who, having sunk in Hell, rises therefrom, takes

  "passage_text": ""'"'Maheswara said, "He who is endued with a liberal disposition, who
honours Brahmanas and treats them with hospitality, who makes gifts of
food and drink and robes and other articles of enjoyment unto the
destitute, the blind, and the distressed, who makes gifts of houses,
erects halls (for use of the public), digs wells, constructs shelters
whence pure and cool water is distributed (during the hot months unto
thirsty travellers), excavates tanks, makes arrangements for the free
distribution of gifts every day, gives to all seekers what each solicits,
who makes gifts of seats and beds and conveyances, wealth, jewels and
gems, houses, all kinds of corn, kine, fields, and women,--verily, he who
always makes these gifts with a cheerful heart, becomes a denizen, O
goddess, of Heaven. He resides there for a long period, enjoying diverse
kinds of superior articles. Passing his time happily in the company of
the Apsaras, he sports in the woods of Nandana and other delightful
regions. After the exhaustion of his merits he falls down from Heaven and
takes birth in the order of humanity, in a family, O goddess, that is
possessed of wealth in abundance and that has a large command of every
article of enjoyments. In that life he becomes endued with all articles
for gratifying his wishes and appetites. Indeed, blessed with the
possession of such articles, he becomes endued with affluence and a
well-filled treasury. The self-born Brahman himself declared it in days
of old that it is even such persons, O goddess, that become highly
blessed and possessed of liberal dispositions and agreeable features.
There are others, O goddess, that are incapable of making gifts. Endued
with small understandings, they cannot make gifts even when solicited by
Brahmanas and possessed of abundant wealth. Beholding the destitute, the
blind, the distressed, and mendicants, and even guests arrived at their
abodes, those persons, always filled with the desire of gratifying the
organ of taste, turn away, even when expressly solicited by them. They
never make gifts of wealth or robes, or viands, or gold, or kine, or any
kind of food. Those men who are disinclined to relieve the distress of
others, who are full of cupidity, who have no faith in the scriptures,
and who never make gifts,--verily, these men of little understanding, O
goddess, have to sink in Hell. In course of time, when their sufferings
in Hell come to an end, they take birth in the order of humanity, in
families that are entirely destitute of wealth. Always suffering from
hunger and thirst, excluded from all decent society, hopeless of ever
enjoying good things, they lead lives of great wretchedness. Born in
families that are destitute of all articles of enjoyment, these men never
succeed in enjoying the good things of the world. Indeed, O goddess, it
is through their acts that persons become wretched and poor. There are
others who are full of arrogance and pride caused by the possession of
riches. Those senseless wretches never offer seats to those that deserve
such an offer. Endued with little understandings they do not give way to
them that deserve such an honour.[575] Nor do they give water for washing
the feet to persons unto whom it should be given. Indeed, they do not
honour, agreeably to the ordinance, with gifts of the Arghya, such
persons as deserve to be honoured therewith. They do not offer water for
washing the mouth unto such as deserve to have that honour. They do not
treat their very preceptors, when the latter arrive at their houses, in
the manner in which preceptors should be treated. Living in cupidity and
arrogance, they refuse to treat their seniors and aged men with love and
affection, even insulting those that deserve to be honoured and asserting
their superiority over them without showing reverence and humility. Such
men, O goddess, sink in Hell. When their sufferings come to an end after
a long course of years, they rise from Hell, and take birth in the order
of humanity, in low and wretched families. Indeed, they who humiliate
their preceptors and seniors, have to take their birth in such castes as
those of Swapakas and Pukkasas who are exceedingly vile and bereft of
