  "passage_text": ""'"'Uma said, "I shall, according to the ordinance, discourse on the
subject of women's duties as far as they are known to me. Do ye all listen
with concentrated attention! The duties of women arise as created at the
outset by kinsmen in the rites of wedding. Indeed, a woman becomes, in
the presence of the nuptial fire, the associate of her lord in the
performance of all righteous deeds.[581] Possessed of a good disposition,
endued with sweet speech, sweet conduct, and sweet features, and always
looking at the face of her husband and deriving as much joy from it as
she does from looking at the face of her child, that chaste woman who
regulates her acts by observing the prescribed restraints, comes to be
regarded as truly righteous in her conduct. Listening (with reverence) to
the duties of wedded life (as expounded in the scriptures), and
accomplishing all those auspicious duties, that woman who regards
righteousness as the foremost of all objects of pursuit, who observes the
same vows as those that are observed by her husband, who adorned with
chastity, looks upon her spouse as a god, who waits upon and serves him
as if he is a god, who surrenders her own will completely to that of her
lord, who is cheerful, who observes excellent vows, who is endued with
good features, and whose heart is completely devoted to her husband so
much that she never thinks even of any other man, is regarded as truly
righteous in conduct. That wife who, even when addressed harshly and
looked upon with angry eyes by her lord, presents a cheerful aspect to
him, is said to be truly devoted to her husband. She who does not cast
her eyes upon the Moon or the Sun or a tree that has a masculine name,
who is adored by her husband and who is possessed of beautiful features,
is regarded as truly righteous. That woman who treats her husband with
the affection which she shows towards her child, even when he (the
husband) happens to be poor or diseased or weak or worn out with the toil
of travelling, is regarded as truly righteous in her conduct. That woman
who is endued with self-control, who has given birth to children, who
serves her husband with devotion, and whose whole heart is devoted to
him, is regarded as truly righteous in her conduct. That woman who waits
upon and serves her lord with a cheerful heart, who is always cheerful of
heart, and who is possessed of humility, is regarded as truly righteous
in her conduct. That woman who always supports her kinsmen and relatives
by giving them food, and whose relish in gratifying her desires or for
articles of enjoyment, or for the affluence of which she is possessed, or
for the happiness with which she is surrounded, falls short of her relish
for her husband, is regarded as truly righteous in her conduct. That
woman who always takes a pleasure in rising at early dawn, who is devoted
to the discharge of all household duties, who always keeps her house
clean, who rubs her house daily with cowdung, who always attends to the
domestic fire (for pouring libations upon it), who never neglects to make
offerings of flowers and other articles to the deities, who with her
husband gratifies the deities and guests and all servants and dependants
of the family with that share of food which is theirs by the ordinances,
and who always takes, according to the ordinance, for herself, what food
remains in the house after the needs have been met of gods and guests and
servants, and who gratifies all people who come in contact with her
family and feed them to their fill, succeeds in acquiring great merit.
That woman who is endued with accomplishments, who gratifies the feet of
her father-in-law and mother-in-law, and who is always devoted to her
father and mother, is regarded as possessed of ascetic wealth. That woman
who supports with food Brahmanas that are weak and helpless, that are
distressed or blind or destitute, comes to be regarded as entitled to
share the merit of her husband. That woman who always observes, with a
light heart, vows that are difficult of observance, whose heart is devoted
to her lord, and who always seeks good of her lord, is regarded as
entitled to share the merits of her husband. Devotion to her lord is
woman's merit; it is her penance; it is her eternal Heaven. Merit,
penances, and Heaven become hers who looks upon her husband as her all in
all, and who, endued with chastity, seeks to devote herself to her lord
in all things. The husband is the god which women have. The husband is
their friend. The husband is their high refuge. Women have no refuge that
can compare with their husbands, and no god that can compare with him.
The husband's grace and Heaven, are equal in the estimation of a woman;
or, if unequal, the inequality is very trivial. O Maheswara, I do not
desire Heaven itself if thou are not satisfied with me. If the husband
that is poor, or diseased or distressed or fallen among foes, or
afflicted by a Brahmana's curse, were to command the wife to accomplish
anything that is improper or unrighteous or that may lead to destruction
of life itself, the wife should, without any hesitation, accomplish it,
guided by the code whose propriety is sanctioned by the law of Distress.
I have thus, O god, expounded, at thy command, what the duties of women
are. Verily, that woman who conducts herself in this way becomes entitled
to a share of the merits won by her husband."'

assembled there, together with all his own attendants. The diverse tribes
of ghostly beings, as also all the embodied Rivers, and the Gandharvas
and Apsaras, all bowed their heads unto Mahadeva and departed for
returning to the places whence they had come.'"'""

Eternal Purusha. Otherwise called Krishna, he is endued with the
splendour of gold, and shines with effulgence like a second sun.
Possessed of ten arms, he is endued with great energy, and is the slayer
of the foes of the gods. Having a whorl on his breast, he has curly locks
of hair on his head. He is worshipped by all the deities. Brahman has
risen from his abdomen. I have sprung from his head, All the luminaries
in the firmament have sprung from his hair. From the bristles on his body
have sprung all the gods and Asuras. From his body have sprung the Rishis
as also all the eternal worlds. He is the veritable abode of the
Grandsire and the abode of all the gods besides. He is the Creator of
this whole Earth, and He is the Lord of the three worlds. He is also the
Destroyer of all creatures mobile and immobile. He is verily the foremost
of all the deities. He is their master. He is the chastiser of all foes.
He is possessed of omniscience. He exists in everything. He is capable of
going everywhere. He is of universal extent (pervading as he does
everything). He is the Supreme Soul. He is the urger of all the senses.
He covers the universe. He is the Supreme Lord. There is nothing in the
three worlds that is superior to him. He is Eternal. He is the slayer of
Madhu, and is otherwise called Govinda. The giver of honours, He will
cause all the kings of Earth to be slain in battle, for achieving the
purposes of the deities, taking birth in a human form. The deities,
abandoned by Him, are unable to accomplish their purposes on earth.
Without obtaining him as their leader they cannot do anything. He is the
leader of all creatures and is adored by all the gods[582]. Within the
abdomen of this Master of the gods who is ever devoted to the
accomplishment of their purposes, of this one who is identical with
Brahma and who is always the refuge of the regenerate Rishis, resides
Brahma (the Grandsire). Indeed, the latter dwells happily in Hari's body
which is the abode. I myself, that am called Sarva, also reside happily
in that happy abode of mine. All the deities too reside in happiness in
His body. Endued with great effulgence, he has eyes that resemble the
petals of the lotus. Sri dwells within Him and He dwells always
associated with her. The bow called Saranga and the discus (called
Sudarsana) are his weapons, together with a sword. He has the enemy of
the snakes (viz., Garuda) sitting on his standard. He is distinguished by
excellent conduct, by purity (of both body and mind), by self-restraint,
by prowess, by energy, by the handsomest form, by tallness and
well-proportioned limbs, by patience, by sincerity, by affluence, by
compassion, by excellence of form, and by might. He shines, endued with
all celestial weapons of wonderful form and make. He has Yoga for his
illusion. He is possessed of a thousand eyes. He is free from every stain
or fault. He is high-minded. He is endued with heroism. He is an object
of pride with all his friends. He is dear to all his kinsmen and
relatives and they are dear to him. He is endued with forgiveness. He is
free from pride or egotism. He is devoted to the Brahmanas and is their
leader. He dispels the fears of all persons afflicted with fear. He
enhances the joys of all his friends. He is the refuge of all creatures.
He is ever engaged in protecting and cherishing the distressed. Possessed
of a thorough acquaintance with all the scriptures, and every kind of
affluence, He is worshipped by all beings. Conversant with all duties,
He is a great benefactor of even enemies when they seek His protection.
Conversant with policy and endued with policy, He is an utterer of Brahma
and has all His senses under perfect control. For doing good to the
deities, Govinda will take birth in the race of the high-souled Manu.
Verily, endued with high intelligence, He will take birth in the
auspicious and righteous race of that Prajapati. Manu will have a son of
the name of Anga. After Anga will come Antardhaman. From Antardhaman will
spring Havirdhaman, that lord of all creatures, free from every stain.
Havirdhaman will have an illustrious son of the name of Rachinavarhi. He

Thunders bellowed, with flashes of lightening.\nThe welkin was enveloped with blue and thick clouds. The deity of the\nclouds then poured pure water like to what he does in the season of\nrains. A thick darkness set in. The points of the compass could no longer\nbe distinguished. Then on that delightful, sacred, and eternal breast of\nthat celestial mountain, the assembled Rishis no longer saw the multitude\nof ghostly beings that associate with Mahadeva. Soon, however, the welkin\ncleared. Some of the Rishis set out for the sacred waters. Others\nreturned whence they came. Verily, beholding that wonderful and\ninconceivable sight, they became filled with amazement. The discourse too\nbetween Sankara and Uma had been heard by them with the feelings, \"That\nforemost of all Beings, of whom the high-souled Sankara spoke to us on\nthat mountain, art Thou. Verily, thou art identical with Eternal Brahma.\nSome time also Mahadeva burnt Himavat with his energy. Thou too hast\nshown us a similar sight of wonder. Indeed, we have been put in\nremembrance of that fact by what we have witnessed today.\" O mighty-armed\nJanardana, I have thus, O puissant one, recited to thee the glory of that\ngod of gods, viz., him that is called Kapardin or Girisa!'\"\n\n\"'Bhishma continued, \"Thus addressed by those denizens of ascetic\nretreats, Krishna, the delighter of Devaki paid due honours unto all\nthose Rishis. Filled with delight, those Rishis once more addressed\nKrishna, saying, 'O slayer of Madhu, do Thou repeatedly show Thyself to\nus at all times! O puissant one, Heaven itself cannot rejoice us so much\nas a right of Thyself. Everything that was said by the illustrious Bhava\n(regarding Thyself) is true. O crusher of foes, we have told Thee all\nabout that mystery. Thou art Thyself conversant with the truth of every\ntopic. Since, however, asked by us, it pleased Thee to ask us in return,\nwe have, for that reason, recited everything (about the discourse of\nBhava with Uma) to Thee for only pleasing Thee. There is nothing in the\nthree worlds that is unknown to Thee. Thou art fully conversant with the\nbirth and origin of all things, indeed, with everything that operates as\na cause (for the production of other objects). In consequence of the\nlightness of our character, we are unable to bear (within ourselves the\nknowledge of) any mystery (without disclosing it).[583] Indeed, in Thy\npresence, O puissant one, we indulge in incoherences from the lightness\nof our hearts. There is no wonderful thing that is unknown to Thee!\nWhatever is on earth, and whatever is in heaven, all is known to Thee! We\ntake our leave of Thee, O Krishna, for returning to our respective abodes.\nMayst Thou increase in intelligence and prosperity! O sire, Thou wilt\nsoon get a son like unto Thee or even more distinguished than Thyself. He\nwill be endued with great energy and splendour. He will achieve great\nfeats, and become possessed of puissance as great as Thine!'\"[584]"

of foes, that it is not right to violate a pledge.[587] All those who
have fallen on the field of battle have really been slain by Time.
Verily, all of us have been slain by Time. Time is, indeed, all-powerful.
Thou art fully conversant with the puissance of Time. Afflicted by Time,
it does not behove thee to grieve. Know that Krishna Himself, otherwise
called Hari, is that Time with blood-red eyes and with club in hand. For
these reasons, O son of Kunti, it does not behove thee to grieve for thy
(slain) kinsfolk. Be thou always free, O delighter of the Kurus, from
grief. Thou hast heard of the glory and greatness of Madhava as recited
by me. That is sufficient for enabling a good man to understand Him.
Having heard the words of Vyasa as also of Narada endued with great
intelligence, I have discoursed to thee on the adorableness of Krishna. I
have myself added, from my own knowledge, something to that discourse.
Verily, I have discoursed also on the surpassing puissance of Krishna as
recited by Mahadeva, unto that conclave of Rishis (on the breast of the
Himavat). The discourse too between Maheswara and the daughter of
Himavat, O Bharata, has been recited by me to thee. He who will bear in
mind that discourse when emanating from a foremost person, he who will
listen to it, and he who will recite it (for other people's hearing), is
sure to win what is highly beneficial. That man will find all his wishes
fulfilled. Departing from this world he will ascend to Heaven. There is
no doubt in this. That man who, desirous of obtaining what is beneficial
for himself, should devote himself to Janardana. O king of the Kurus, it
behoves thee also to always bear in mind those incidents of duty and
righteousness which were declared by Maheswara. If thou conduct thyself
according to those precepts, if thou bear the rod of chastisement
rightly, if thou protect thy subjects properly, thou mayst be sure of
attaining to heaven. It behoves thee, O king, to protect thy subjects"

He that is armed with a car-wheel; He that is\nincapable of being agitated; He that is armed with all kinds of weapons\n(CMXCIII--M). Om, salutations to Him!\n\n\"Even thus have I recited to thee, without any exception, the thousand\nexcellent names of the high-souled Kesava whose glory should always be\nsung. That man who hears the names every day or who recites them every\nday, never meets with any evil either here or hereafter. If a Brahmana\ndoes this he succeeds in mastering the Vedanta; if a Kshatriya does it,\nhe becomes always successful in battle. A Vaisya, by doing it, becomes\npossessed of affluence, while a Sudra earns great happiness. If one\nbecomes desirous of earning the merit of righteousness, one succeeds in\nearning it (by hearing or reciting these names). If it is wealth that one\ndesires, one succeeds in earning wealth (by acting in this way). So also\nthe man who wishes for enjoyments of the senses succeeds in enjoying all\nkinds of pleasures, and the man desirous of offspring acquires offspring\n(by pursuing this course of conduct). That man who with devotion and\nperseverance and heart wholly turned towards him, recites these thousand\nnames of Vasudeva every day, after having purified himself, succeeds in\nacquiring great fame, a position of eminence among his kinsmen, enduring\nprosperity, and lastly, that which is of the highest benefit to him\n(viz., emancipation itself). Such a man never meets with fear at any\ntime, and acquires great prowess and energy. Disease never afflicts him;\nsplendour of complexion, strength, beauty, and accomplishments become\nhis. The sick become hale, the afflicted become freed from their\nafflictions; the affrighted become freed from fear, and he that is\nplunged in calamity becomes freed from calamity. The man who hymns the\npraises of that foremost of Beings by reciting His thousand names with\ndevotion succeeds in quickly crossing all difficulties. That mortal who\ntakes refuge in Vasudeva and who becomes devoted to Him, becomes freed of\nall sins and attains to eternal Brahma. They who are devoted to Vasudeva\nhave never to encounter any evil. They become freed from the fear of\nbirth, death, decrepitude, and disease. That man who with devotion and\nfaith recites this hymn (consisting of the thousand names of Vasudeva)\nsucceeds in acquiring felicity of soul, forgiveness of disposition,\nProsperity, intelligence, memory, and fame. Neither wrath, nor jealousy,\nnor cupidity, nor evil understanding ever appears in those men of\nrighteousness who are devoted to that foremost of beings. The firmament\nwith the sun, moon and stars, the welkin, the points of the compass, the\nearth and the ocean, are all held and supported by the prowess of the\nhigh-souled Vasudeva. The whole mobile and immobile universe with the\ndeities, Asuras, and Gandharvas, Yakshas, Uragas and Rakshasas, is under\nthe sway of Krishna. The senses, mind, understanding, life, energy,\nstrength and memory, it has been said, have Vasudeva for their soul.\nIndeed, this body that is called Kshetra, and the intelligent soul\nwithin, that is called the knower of Kshetra, also have Vasudeva for\ntheir soul. Conduct (consisting of practices) is said to be the foremost\nof all topics treated of in the scriptures. Righteousness has conduct for\nits basis. The unfading Vasudeva is said to be the lord of righteousness.\nThe Rishis, the Pitris, the deities, the great (primal) elements, the\nmetals, indeed, the entire mobile and immobile universe, has sprung from\nNarayana. Yoga, the Sankhya Philosophy, knowledge, all mechanical arts,\nthe Vedas, the diverse scriptures, and all learning, have sprung from\nJanardana. Vishnu is the one great element or substance which has spread\nitself out into multifarious forms. Covering the three worlds, He the\nsoul of all things, enjoys them all. His glory knows no diminution, and\nHe it is that is the Enjoyer of the universe (as its Supreme Lord). This\nhymn in praise of the illustrious Vishnu composed by Vyasa, should be\nrecited by that person who wishes to acquire happiness and that which is\nthe highest benefit (viz., emancipation). Those persons that worship and\nadore the Lord of the universe, that deity who is inborn and possessed of\nblazing effulgence, who is the origin or cause of the universe, who knows\non deterioration, and who is endued with eyes that are as large and\nbeautiful as the petals of the lotus, have never to meet with any\ndiscomfiture.\"'\""

immediately of all his sins. Hear, O sinless one, as I recite to thee the

Durvasa,--these are endued with severe penance and great self-restraint,
and are celebrated over the three worlds. There are others who are equal
to Rudra himself. They live in the region of Brahman. By naming them with
reverence a sonless man obtains a son, and a poor man obtains wealth.
Indeed, by naming them, one acquires success in religion, and wealth and
pleasure. One should also take the name of that celebrated king who was
Emperor of all the earth and equal to a Prajapati, viz., that foremost of
monarchs, Prithu, the son of Vena. The earth became his daughter (from
love and affection). One should also name Pururavas of the Solar race and
equal unto Mahendra himself in prowess. He was the son of Ila and
celebrated over the three worlds. One should, indeed, take the name of
that dear son of Vudha. One should also take the name of Bharata, that
hero celebrated over the three worlds. He also who in the Krita age
adored the gods in a grand Gomedha sacrifice, viz., Rantideva of great
splendour, who was equal unto Mahadeva himself, should be named. Endued
with penances, possessed of every auspicious mark, the source of every
kind of benefit to the world, he was the conqueror of the universes. One
should also take the name of the royal sage Sweta of illustrious fame. He
had gratified the great Mahadeva and it was for his sake that Andhaka was
slain. One should also take the name of the royal sage Bhagiratha of
great fame, who, through the grace of Mahadeva, succeeded in bringing
down the sacred river from heaven (for flowing over the earth and
cleansing all human beings of their sins). It was Bhagiratha who caused
the ashes of the sixty thousand sons of Sagara to be overflowed with the
sacred waters of Ganga and thereby rescued them from their sin. Indeed,
one should take the names of all these that were endued with the blazing
effulgence of fire, great beauty of person, and high energy. Some of them

Indeed, at\nsuch places, there can be no fear of the king, nor of Pisachas and\nRakshasas.[607] Verily, the man who recites these Mantras ceases to have\nany fear of fire or water or wind or beasts of prey. These Savitri\nMantras, recited duly, contribute to the peace and well-being of all the\nfour orders. Those men who recite them with reverence become freed from\nevery sorrow and at last attain to a high end. Even these are the results\nachieved by them that recite these Savitri Mantras which are of the form\nof Brahma. That man who recites these Mantras in the midst of kine sees\nhis kine become fruitful. Whether when setting out on a journey, or\nentering a house on coming back, one should recite these Mantras on every\noccasion. These Mantras constitute a great mystery of the Rishis and are\nthe very highest of those which they silently recite. Even such are these\nMantras unto them who practise the duty of recitation and pour libations\non the sacrificial fire. This that I have said unto thee is the excellent\nopinion of Parasara. It was recited in former days unto Sakra himself.\nRepresenting as it does Truth or Eternal Brahman, I have declared it in\nfull to thee. It constitutes that heart of all creatures, and is the\nhighest Sruti. All the princes of the race of Soma and of Surya, viz.,\nthe Raghavas and the Kauravas, recite these Mantras every day after\nhaving purified themselves, These constitute the highest end of human\ncreatures. There is rescue from every trouble and calamity in the daily\nrecitation of the names of the deities of the seven Rishis, and of\nDhruva. Indeed, such recitation speedily frees one from distress. The\nsages of olden times, viz., Kasyapa, Gotama, and others, and Bhrigu\nAngiras and Atri and others, and Sukra, Agastya, and Vrihaspati, and\nothers, all of whom are regenerate Rishis, have adored these Mantras.\nApproved of by the son of Bharadwaja, these Mantras were attained by the\nsons of Richika. Verily, having acquired them again from Vasishtha, Sakra\nand the Vasus went forth to battle and succeeded in subjugating the\nDanavas. That man who makes a present of a hundred kine with their horns\ncovered with plates of gold unto a Brahmana possessed of much learning\nand well-conversant with the Vedas, and he who causes the excellent\nBharata story to be recited in his house every day, are said to acquire\nequal merits. By reciting the name of Bhrigu one's righteousness becomes\nenhanced. By bowing to Vasishtha one's energy become enhanced. By bowing\nunto Raghu, one becomes victorious in battle. By reciting the praises of\nthe Aswins, one becomes freed from diseases. I have thus, O king, told\nthee of the Savitri Mantras which are identical with eternal Brahman.   "passage_text": "SECTION CLI\n\n\"'Yudhishthira said, \"Who deserve to be worshipped? Who are they unto whom\nwe should bow? How, indeed, should we behave towards whom? What course of\nconduct, O grandsire, towards what classes of persons is regarded\nfaultless?\"\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"The humiliation of Brahmanas would humiliate the very\ndeities. By bowing unto Brahmanas one does not, O Yudhishthira, incur any\nfault. They deserve to be worshipped. They deserve to have our\nsalutations. Thou shouldst behave towards them as if they are thy sons.\nIndeed, it is those men endued with great wisdom that uphold all the\nworlds. The Brahmanas are the great causeways of Righteousness in respect\nof all the worlds. Their happiness consists in renouncing all kinds of\nwealth. They are devoted to the vow of restraining speech. They are\nagreeable to all creatures, and observant of diverse excellent vows. They\nare the refuge of all creatures in the universe. They are the authors of\nall the regulations which govern the worlds. They are possessed of great\nfame. Penances are always their great wealth. Their power consists in\nspeech. Their energy flows from the duties they observe. Conversant with\nall duties, they are possessed of minute vision, so that they are\ncognizant of the subtlest considerations. They are of righteous desires.\nThey live the observance of well-performed duties. They are the causeways\nof Righteousness. The four kinds of living creatures exist, depending\nupon them as their refuge. They are the path or road along which all\nshould go. They are the guides of all. They are the eternal upholders of\nall the sacrifices. They always uphold the heavy burdens of sires and\ngrandsires. They never droop under heavy weights even when passing along\ndifficult roads like strong cattle. They are attentive to the\nrequirements of Pitris and deities and guests. They are entitled to eat\nthe first portions of Havya and Kavya. By the very food they eat, they\nrescue the three worlds from great fear. They are as it were, the Island\n(for refuge) for all worlds. They are the eyes of all persons endued with\nsight. The wealth they possess consists of all the branches of knowledge\nknown by the name of Siksha and all the Srutis. Endued with great skill,\nthey are conversant with the most subtle relations of things. They are\nwell-acquainted with the end of all things, and their thoughts are always\nemployed upon the science of the soul. They are endued with the knowledge\nof the beginning, the middle, and the end of all things, and they are\npersons in whom doubts no longer exist in consequence of feeling certain\nof their knowledge. They are fully aware of the distinctions between what\nis superior and what is inferior. They it is who attain to the highest\nend. Freed from all attachments, cleansed of all sins, transcending all\npairs of opposites (such as heat and cold, happiness and misery, etc.),\nthey are unconnected with all worldly things. Deserving of every honour,\nthey are always held in great esteem by persons endued with knowledge and\nhigh souls. They cast equal eyes on sandal-paste and filth or dirt, on\nwhat is food and what is not food. They see with an equal eye their brown\nvestments of coarse cloth and fabrics of silk and animal skins. They\nwould live for many days together without eating any food, and dry up\ntheir limbs by such abstention from all sustenance. They devote\nthemselves earnestly to the study of the Vedas, restraining their senses.\nThey would make gods of those that are not gods, and not gods of those\nthat are gods. Enraged, they can create other worlds and other Regents of\nthe worlds than those that exist. Through the course of those high-souled\nones, the ocean became so saline as to be undrinkable. The fire of their\nwrath yet burns in the forest of Dandaka, unquenched by time. They are\nthe gods of the gods, and the cause of all cause. They are the authority\nof all authorities. What man of intelligence and wisdom is there that\nwould seek to humiliate them? Amongst them the young and the old all\ndeserve honours. They honour one another (not in consequence of\ndistinctions of age but) in consequence of distinctions in respect of\npenances and knowledge. Even the Brahmana that is destitute of knowledge\nis a god and is a high instrument for cleansing others. He amongst them,\nthen, that is possessed of knowledge is a much higher god and like unto\nthe ocean when full (to the brim). Learned or unlearned, Brahmana is\nalways a high deity. Sanctified or unsanctified (with the aid of\nMantras), Fire is ever a great deity. A blazing fire even when it burns\non a crematorium, is not regarded as tainted in consequence of the\ncharacter of the spot whereon it burns. Clarified butter looks beautiful\nwhether kept on the sacrificial altar or in a chamber. So, if a Brahmana\nbe always engaged in evil acts, he is still to be regarded as deserving\nof honour. Indeed, know that the Brahmana is always a high deity.\"'\""
}

  "passage_text": "SECTION CLII\n\n\"'Yudhishthira said, \"Tell us, O king, what is that reward attached to the\nworship of Brahmanas, seeing which thou worshippest them, O thou of\nsuperior intelligence! Indeed, what is that success, flowing from their\nworship, guided by which thou worshippest them?\"\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"In this connection is cited this old narrative of a\nconversation between Pavana and Arjuna, O Bharata! Endued with a thousand\narms and great beauty the mighty Kartavirya, in days of yore, became the\nlord of all the world. He had his capital in the city of Mahishmati. Of\nunbaffled prowess, that chief of the Haihaya race of Kshatriyas swayed\nthe whole earth with her belt of seas, together with all her islands and\nall her precious mines of gold and gems. Keeping before him the duties of\nthe Kshatriya order, as also humility and Vedic knowledge, the king made\nlarge gifts of wealth unto the Rishi Dattatreya. Indeed, the son of\nKritavirya thus adored the great ascetic who, becoming pleased with him,\nasked him to solicit three boons. Thus requested by the Rishi in respect\nof boons, the king addressed him, saying, 'Let me become endued with a\nthousand arms when I am in the midst of my troops. While, however, I\nremain at home let me have, as usual only two arms! Indeed, let\ncombatants, when engaged in battle, behold me possessed of a thousand\narms, observant also of high vows, let me succeed in subjugating the\nwhole earth by dint of my prowess. Having acquired the earth righteously,\nlet me sway her with vigilance. There is a fourth boon which, O foremost\nof regenerate persons, I solicit thee to grant. O faultless one, in\nconsequence of the disposition to favour me, it behoveth thee to grant it\nto me. Dependent that I am on thee, whenever I may happen to go wrong,\nlet the righteous come forth to instruct and set me right!' Thus\naddressed, the Brahmana replied unto the king, saying, 'So let it be!'\nEven thus were those boons acquired by that king of blazing effulgence.\nRiding then on his car whose splendour resembled that of fire or the Sun,\nthe monarch, blinded by his great prowess, said, 'Who, indeed, is there\nthat can be regarded as my equal in patience and energy, in fame and\nheroism, in prowess and strength?' After he had uttered these words, an\ninvisible voice in the welkin said, 'O ignorant wretch, dost thou not\nknow that the Brahmana is superior to the Kshatriya? The Kshatriya,\nassisted by the Brahmana rules all creatures!'\n\n\"'\"Arjuna said, 'When gratified, I am able to create many creatures. When\nangry, I am able to destroy all. In thought, word, and deed, I am the\nforemost. The Brahmana is certainly not above me! The first proposition\nhere is that the Brahmana is superior to the Kshatriya. The\ncounter-proposition is that the Kshatriya is superior. Thou hast said, O\ninvisible being that the two are united together (in the act upon which\nthe Kshatriya's superiority is sought to be based). A distinction,\nhowever, is observable in this. It is seen that Brahmanas take refuge\nwith Kshatriyas. The Kshatriyas never seek the refuge of Brahmanas.\nIndeed, throughout the earth, the Brahmanas, accepting such refuge under\nthe pretence of teaching the Vedas, draw their sustenance from the\nKshatriyas. The duty of protecting all creatures is vested in Kshatriyas.\nIt is from the Kshatriyas that the Brahmanas derive their sustenance. How\nthen can the Brahmana be superior to the Kshatriyas? Well, I shall from\ntoday, bring under my subjection, your Brahmanas who are superior to all\ncreatures but who have mendicancy for their occupation and who are so\nself-conceited! What the virgin Gayatri has said from the welkin is not\ntrue. Robed in skins, the Brahmanas move about in independence. I shall\nbring those independent wights under my subjection. Deity or man, there\nis none in the three worlds who can hurl me from the sovereignty I enjoy.\nHence, I am certainly superior to the Brahmanas. This world that is now\nregarded as having Brahmanas for its foremost denizens shall soon be made\nsuch as to have Kshatriyas for its foremost denizens. There is none that\nis capable of bearing my might in battle!' Hearing these words of Arjuna,\nthe welkin-ranging goddess became agitated. Then the god of wind,\naddressing the king from the sky, said, 'Cast off this sinful attitude.\nBow unto the Brahmanas. By injuring them thou wilt bring about troubles\non thy kingdom. The Brahmanas will either slay thee, king though thou\nart, or, endued with great might that they are, they will drive thee away\nfrom thy kingdom, despoiling thee of thy energy!' The king, hearing this\nspeech, addressed the speaker, saying, 'Who, indeed, art thou?' The god of\nwind answered, 'I am the god of wind and the messenger of the deities! I\nsay unto thee what is for thy benefit.'\n\n\"'\"Arjuna said, 'Oh, I see that thou hast today shown thy devotion and\nattachment to the Brahmanas. Tell me now what kind of earthly creature is\nthe Brahmana! Tell me, does a superior Brahmana resemble the Wind in any\nrespect? Or, is he like Water, or Fire, or the Sun, or the Firmament?'\"'\""
}

"'"The god of wind said, 'Once on a time, O king, a ruler of the name of
Anga desired to give away the whole earth as sacrificial present unto the
Brahmanas. At this, the earth became filled with anxiety. "I am the
daughter of Brahman. I hold all creatures. Having obtained me, alas, why
does this foremost of kings wish to give me away unto the Brahmanas?
Abandoning my character as the soil, I shall now repair to the presence
of my sire. Let this king with all his kingdom meet with destruction."
Arrived at this conclusion, she departed for the region of Brahman. The
Rishi Kasyapa, beholding goddess Earth on the point of departing, himself
immediately entered the visible embodiment of the goddess, casting off
his own body, by the aid of Yoga. The earth thus penetrated by the spirit
of Kasyapa, grew in prosperity and became full of all kinds of vegetable
produce. Indeed, O king for the time that Kasyapa pervaded the earth,
Righteousness became foremost everywhere and all fears ceased. In this
way, O king, the earth remained penetrated by the spirit of Kasyapa for
thirty thousand celestial years, fully alive to all those functions which
it used to discharge while it was penetrated by the spirit of Brahman's
daughter. Upon the expiry of this period, the goddess returned from the
region of Brahman and arrived here bowed unto Kasyapa and from that time
became the daughter of that Rishi. Kasyapa is a Brahmana. Even this was
the feat, O king, that a Brahmana did. Tell me the name of the Kshatriya
who can be held to be superior to Kasyapa!' Hearing these words, king
Arjuna remained silent. Unto him the god of wind once more said, 'Hear
now, O king, the story of Utathya who was born in the race of Angiras.
The daughter of Soma, named Bhadra, came to be regarded as unrivalled in
beauty. Her sire Soma regarded Utathya to be the fittest of husbands for
her. The famous and highly blessed maiden of faultless limbs, observing
diverse vows, underwent the severest austerities from the desire of
obtaining Utathya for her lord. After a while, Soma's father Atri,
inviting Utathya to his house, bestowed upon him the famous maiden.
Utathya, who used to give away sacrificial presents in copious measure,
duly received the girl for his wife. It so happened, however, that the
handsome Varuna had, from a long time before, coveted the girl. Coming to
the woods where Utathya dwelt, Varuna stole away the girl when she had
plunged into the Yamuna for a bath. Abducting her thus, the Lord of the
waters took her to his own abode. That mansion was of a wonderful aspect.
It was adorned with six hundred thousand lakes. There is no mansion that
can be regarded more beautiful than that palace of Varuna. It was adorned
with many palaces and by the presence of diverse tribes of Apsaras and of
diverse excellent articles of enjoyment. There, within that palace, the
Lord of waters, O king, sported with the damsel. A little while after,
the fact of the ravishment of his wife was reported to Utathya. Indeed,
having heard all the facts from Narada, Utathya addressed the celestial
Rishi, saying, "Go, O Narada, unto Varuna and speak with due severity
unto him. Ask him as to why he has abducted my wife, and, indeed, tell
him in my name that he should yield her up. Thou mayst say to him
further, 'Thou are a protector of the worlds, O Varuna, and not a
destroyer! Why then hast thou abducted Utathya's wife bestowed upon him
by Soma?'" Thus requested by Utathya, the celestial Rishi Narada repaired
to where Varuna was and addressing him, said, "Do thou set free the wife
of Utathya. Indeed, why hast thou abducted her?" Hearing these words of
Narada, Varuna replied unto him, saying, "This timid girl is exceedingly
dear to me. I dare not let her go!" Receiving this reply, Narada repaired
to Utathya and cheerlessly said, "O great ascetic, Varuna has driven me
out from his house, seizing me by the throat. He is unwilling to restore
to thee thy spouse. Do thou act as thou pleasest." Hearing these words of
Narada, Angiras became inflamed with wrath. Endued with wealth of
penances, he solidified the waters and drank them off, aided by his
energy. When all the waters were thus drunk off, the Lord of that element
became very cheerless with all his friends and kinsfolk. For all that, he
did not still give up Utathya's wife. Then Utathya, that foremost of
regenerate persons, filled with wrath, commanded Earth, saying, "O
amiable one, do thou show land where there are at present the six hundred
thousand lakes." At these words of the Rishi, the Ocean receded from the
spot indicated, and land appeared which was exceedingly sterile. Unto the
rivers that flowed through that region, Utathya said, "O Saraswati, do
thou become invisible here. Indeed, O timid lady, leaving this region, go
thou to the desert! O auspicious goddess, let this region, destitute of
thee, cease to become sacred." When that region (in which the lord of
waters dwelt) became dry, he repaired to Angiras, taking with him
Utathya's spouse, and made her over to him. Getting back his wife,
Utathya became cheerful. Then, O chief of the Haihaya race, that great
Brahmana rescued both the universe and the Lord of waters from the
situation of distress into which he had brought them. Conversant with
every duty, the Rishi Utathya of great energy, after getting back his
spouse, O king, said so unto Varuna, "I have recovered my wife, O Lord of
waters, with the aid of my penances and after inflicting such distress on
thee as made thee cry aloud in anguish!" Having said this, he went home,
with that wife of his. Even such, O king, was Utathya, that foremost of
Brahmanas. Shall I go on? Or, will you yet persist in thy opinion? What,
is there a Kshatriya that is superior to Utathya?'"'""
}

  "passage_text": "SECTION CLV\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"Thus addressed, king Arjuna remained silent. The god of\nwind once more spoke to him, 'Listen now, O king, to the story of the\ngreatness of the Brahmana Agastya. Once on a time, the gods were\nsubjugated by the Asuras upon which they became very cheerless. The\nsacrifices of the deities were all seized, and the Swadha of the Pitris\nwas also misappropriated. Indeed, O Chief of the Haihayas, all the\nreligious acts and observances of human beings also were suspended by the\nDanavas. Divested of their prosperity, the deities wandered over the\nearth as we have heard. One day, in course of their wandering they met\nAgastya of high vows, that Brahmana, O king, who was endued with great\nenergy and splendour which was as blazing as that of the sun. Saluting\nhim duly, the deities made the usual enquiries of politeness. They then,\nO King, said these words unto that high-souled one, \"We have been\ndefeated by the Danavas in battle and have, therefore, fallen off from\naffluence and prosperity. Do thou, therefore, O foremost of ascetics,\nrescue us from this situation of great fear.\" Thus informed of the plight\nto which the deities had been reduced, Agastya became highly incensed\n(with the Danavas). Possessed of great energy, he at once blazed forth\nlike the all-consuming fire at the time of the universal dissolution.\nWith the blazing rays that then emanated from the Rishi, the Danavas\nbegan to be burnt. Indeed, O king, thousands of them began to drop down\nfrom the sky. Burning with the energy of Agastya, the Danavas, abandoning\nboth heaven and earth, fled towards the southern direction. At that time\nthe Danava king Vali was performing a Horse-sacrifice in the nether\nregions. Those great Asuras who were with him in those regions or who\nwere dwelling in the bowels of the earth, were not burnt. The deities,\nupon the destruction of their foes, then regained their own regions,\ntheir fears entirely dispelled. Encouraged by what he accomplished for\nthem, they then solicited the Rishi to destroy those Asuras who had taken\nrefuge within the bowels of the earth or in the nether regions. Thus\nsolicited by the gods, Agastya replied unto them, saying, \"Yes, I am\nfully competent to consume those Asuras that are dwelling underneath the\nearth; but if I achieve such a feat, my penances will suffer a\ndiminution. Hence, I shall not exert my power.\" Even thus, O king, were\nthe Danavas consumed by the illustrious Rishi with his own energy. Even\nthus did Agastya of cleansed soul, O monarch, accomplish that feat with\nthe aid of his penances. O sinless one, even so was Agastya as described\nby me! Shall I continue? Or, will you say anything in reply? Is there any\nKshatriya who is greater than Agastya?'\"\n\n\"'Bhishma continued, \"Thus addressed, king Arjuna remained silent. The god\nof wind once more said, 'Hear, O king, one of the great feats of the\nillustrious Vasishtha. Once on a time the deities were engaged in\nperforming a sacrifice on the shores of the lake Vaikhanasa. Knowing of\nhis puissance, the sacrificing gods thought of Vasishtha and made him\ntheir priest in imagination. Meanwhile, seeing the gods reduced and\nemaciated in consequence of the Diksha they were undergoing, a race of\nDanavas, of the name of Khalins, of statures as gigantic as mountains,\ndesired to slay them. Those amongst the Danavas that were either disabled\nor slain in the fight were plunged into the waters of the Manasa lake and\nin consequence of the boon of the Grandsire they instantly came back to\nvigour and life. Taking up huge and terrible mountain summits and maces\nand trees, they agitated the waters of the lake, causing them to swell up\nto the height of a hundred yojanas. They then ran against the deities\nnumbering ten thousand. Afflicted by the Danavas, the gods then sought\nthe protection of their chief, Vasava. Sakra, however, was soon afflicted\nby them. In his distress he sought the protection of Vasishtha. At this,\nthe holy Rishi Vasishtha assured the deities, dispelling their fears.\nUnderstanding that the gods had become exceedingly cheerless, the ascetic\ndid this through compassion. He put forth his energy and burnt, without\nany exertion, those Danavas called Khalins. Possessed of wealth of\npenances, the Rishi brought the River Ganga, who had gone to Kailasa, to\nthat spot. Indeed, Ganga appeared, piercing through the waters of the\nlake. The lake was penetrated by that river. And as that celestial\nstream, piercing through the waters of the lake, appeared, it flowed on,\nunder the name of Sarayu. The place whereon those Danavas fell came to be\ncalled after them. Even thus were the denizens of Heaven, with Indra at\ntheir head, rescued from great distress by Vasishtha, It was thus that\nthose Danavas, who had received boons from Brahman, were slain by that\nhigh-souled Rishi. O sinless one, I have narrated to thee the feat which\nVasishtha accomplished. Shall I go on? Or, will you say anything! Was\nthere a Kshatriya who could be said to surpass the Brahmana Vasishtha?'\"'\""
}

The gods,\noverwhelmed by darkness, began to fall before the mighty Danavas, O\nforemost of kings! Repeatedly struck by the Asuras, the denizens of\nheaven began to lose their strength. They then beheld the learned\nBrahmana Atri, endued with wealth of penances, engaged in the observance\nof austerities. Addressing that Rishi who had conquered all his senses\nand in whom wrath had been extinguished, they said \"Behold, O Rishi,\nthese two, viz., Soma and Surya, who have both been pierced by the Asuras\nwith their arrows! In consequence of this, darkness has overtaken us, and\nwe are being struck down by the foe. We do not see the end of our\ntroubles! Do thou, O lord of great puissance, rescue us from this great\nfear.\"\n\n\"'\"'The Rishi said, \"How, indeed, shall I protect you?\" They answered,\nsaying, \"Do thou thyself become Chandramas. Indeed, in consequence\nof his agreeable disposition, he began to look as handsome and delightful\nas Soma himself. Even this was the feat that regenerate one, aided by his\nsacred fire,--that silent reciter of Mantras, that one clad in\ndeer-skins,--accomplished! Behold, O royal sage, that act achieved by\nthat Rishi who subsisted upon fruits only! I have thus narrated to thee,\nin detail, the feat of the high-souled Atri. Shall I go on? Or, will you\nsay anything? Is there a Kshatriya that is superior to this regenerate\nRishi?'\n\n\"'\"Thus addressed, Arjuna remained silent. Whatever other behest thou mayst be pleased to utter, O learned\nBrahmana, we are ready to accomplish.\"\n\n\"'\"'Chyavana said, \"The twin Aswins shall drink Soma with all of you! Both\nof them are gods, O chief of the deities, for they are the sons of Surya.\nLet the gods do what I have said. By acting according to those words, the\ngods will reap great advantage. By acting otherwise, evil will overtake\nthem.\"\n\n\"'\"'Indra said, \"I shall not, O foremost of regenerate persons, drink Soma\nwith the Aswins! Let others drink with them as they please! As regards\nmyself, I dare not do it.\"\n\n\"'\"'Chyavana said, \"If, O slayer of Vala, thou wilt not obey my words, thou\nshalt, this very day, drink Soma with them in sacrifice, compelled by me!\""

  "passage_text": "SECTION CLVII

"'Bhishma said, "Hearing these words of the god of wind, Arjuna remained
silent. At this, the god of wind once more addressed him, saying, 'When
the denizens of heaven, with Indra at their head, found themselves within
the mouth of the Asura Mada, at that time Chyavana took away from them
the earth. Deprived previously of heaven and now shorn of the earth also,
the gods became very cheerless. Indeed, those high-souled ones, afflicted
with grief, then threw themselves unreservedly upon the Grandsire's
protection.'

"'"'The gods said, "O thou that art adored by all creatures of the
universe, the earth has been taken away from us by Chyavana, while we have
been deprived of heaven by the Kapas, O puissant one!"

"'"'Brahman said, "Ye denizens of heaven, do you, with Indra at your head,
repair quickly and seek the protection of the Brahmanas. By gratifying
them you will succeed in regaining both the regions as before." Thus
instructed by the Grandsire, the deities repaired to the Brahmanas and
became suppliants for their protection. The Brahmanas replied, enquiring,
"Whom shall we subjugate?" Thus asked, the deities said unto them, "Do ye
subjugate the Kapas." The Brahmanas then said, "Bringing them down on the
earth first, we shall speedily subjugate them." After this, the Brahmanas
commenced a rite having for its object the destruction of the Kapas. As
soon as this was heard of by the Kapas, they immediately despatched a
messenger of theirs, named Dhanin, unto those Brahmanas. Dhanin, coming
to them as they sat on the earth, thus delivered to them the message of
the Kapas. "The Kapas are even like you all! (They are not inferior to any
of you). Hence, what will be the effect of these rites which you seem to
be bent upon achieving? All of them are well-conversant with the Vedas
and possessed of wisdom. All of them are mindful of sacrifices. All of
them have Truth for their vow, and for these reasons all of them are
regarded as equal to great Rishis. The goddess of Prosperity sports among
them, and they, in their turn, support her with reverence. They never
indulge in acts of fruitless congress with their wives, and they never
eat the flesh of such animals as have not been killed in sacrifices. They
pour libations on the blazing sacrificial fire (every day) and are
obedient to the behests of their preceptors and seniors. All of them are
of souls under perfect control, and never take any food without dividing
it duly among their children. They always proceed on cars and other
vehicles together (without any of them riding his own vehicle while
others journey on foot). They never indulge in acts of congress with
their spouses when the latter are in midst of their functional period.
They all act in such a way as to attain to regions of felicity hereafter.
Indeed, they are always righteous in their deeds. When women quick with
child or old men have not eaten, they never eat anything themselves. They
never indulge in play or sports of any kind in the forenoon. They never
sleep during the day. When the Kapas have these and many other virtues
and accomplishments, why, indeed, would you seek to subjugate them? You
should abstain from the endeavour! Verily, by such abstention ye would
achieve what is for your good."

"'"'The Brahmanas said, "Oh, we shall subjugate the Kapas! In this matter,
we art one with the deities. Hence, the Kapas deserve slaughter at your
hands. As regards Dhanin, he should return whence he came!" After this,
Dhanin, returning to the Kapas, said unto them, "The Brahmanas are not
disposed to do you any good!" Hearing this, all the Kapas took up their
weapons and proceeded towards the Brahmanas. The Brahmanas, beholding the
Kapas advancing against them with the standards of their cars upraised,
forthwith created certain blazing fires for the destruction of the Kapas.
Those eternal fires, created with the aid of Vedic Mantras, having
effected the destruction of the Kapas, began to shine in the firmament
like so many (golden) clouds. The gods, having assembled together in
battle, slew many of the Danavas. They did not know at that time that it
was the Brahmanas who had effected their destruction. Then Narada of
great energy, coming there, O king, informed the deities how their foes,
the Kapas, had been really slain by the Brahmanas of mighty energy (and
not by deities themselves). Hearing these words of Narada, the denizens
of heaven became highly gratified. They also applauded those regenerate
allies of theirs that were possessed of great fame. The energy and
prowess of the deities then began to increase, and worshipped in all the
worlds, they acquired also the boon of immortality!' After the god of
wind had said these words, king Arjuna worshipped him duly and addressing
him answered in these words. Hear, O mighty armed monarch, what Arjuna
said.

"'"Arjuna said, 'O puissant god, always and by all means do I live for the
Brahmanas! Devoted to them, I worship them always! Through the grace of
Dattatreya I have obtained this might of mine! Through his grace have I
been able to accomplish great feats in the world and achieve high merit!
Oh, I have, with attention, heard of the achievements, O god of the wind,
of the Brahmanas with all their interesting details as recited by thee
truly.'

"'"The god of wind said, 'Do thou protect and cherish the Brahmanas, in the
exercise of those Kshatriya duties which are thine by birth. Do thou
protect them even as thou protectest thy own senses! There is danger to
thee from the race of Bhrigu! All that, however, will take place on a
distant day.'"'""
}

Krishna who became the mighty Boar and raised the submerged Earth. It is

mountains. Below Him are the welkin, heaven, the four cardinal points,
and the four subsidiary points. It is from him that the entire creation
has flowed. It is He who has created this ancient universe. In His navel
appeared a Lotus. Within that Lotus sprang Brahma himself of immeasurable

age, O Partha, Krishna existed (on the earth), in the form of
Righteousness. In the Treta age, he existed in the form of Knowledge. In

takes birth in the race of either the gods or among men. Staying on
Righteousness, this Krishna of cleansed soul (on such occasion) protects
both the higher and the lower worlds. Sparing those that deserve to be
spared, Krishna sets himself to the slaughter of the Asura, O Partha! It
is he who is all acts proper and improper and it is he who is the cause.
It is Krishna who is the act done, the act to be done, and the act that
is being done. Know that that illustrious one is Rahu and Soma and Sakra.
It is he that is Viswakarma. It is he that is of universal form. He is
the destroyer and he is the Creator of the universe. He is the wielder of
the Sula (lance); He is of human form; and He is of terrible form. All
creatures sing his praises, for he is known by his acts. Hundreds of
Gandharvas and Apsaras and deities always accompany him. The very
Rakshasas hymn his praise. He is the Enhancer of Wealth; He is the one
victorious Being in the universe. In Sacrifices, eloquent men hymn His
praises. The singers of Samans praise Him by reciting the Rathantaras.
The Brahmanas praise Him with Vedic Mantras. It is unto Him that the
sacrificial priests pour their libations. The deities with Indra at their
head hymned His praise when He lifted up the Gobardhana mountains for
protecting the cow-herds of Brindavana against the incessant showers that
Indra poured in rage. He is, O Bharata, the one Blessing unto all
creatures. He, O Bharata, having entered the old Brahma cave, beheld from
that place the original cover of the world in the beginning of Time.[613]
Agitating all the Danavas and the Asuras, this Krishna of foremost feats
rescued the earth. It is unto Him that people dedicate diverse kinds of
food. It is unto Him that the warriors dedicate all kinds of their
vehicles at the time of war. He is eternal, and it is under that
illustrious one that the welkin, earth, heaven, all things exist and
stay. He it is who has caused the vital seed of the gods Mitra and Varuna
to fall within a jar, whence sprang the Rishi known by the name of
Vasishtha. It is Krishna who is the god of wind; it is He who is the
puissant Aswins; it is He who is that first of gods, viz., the sun
possessed of a thousand rays. It is He by whom the Asuras have been
subjugated. It is He who covered the three worlds with three steps of
His. He is the soul of the deities and human beings, and Pitris. It is He
who is the Sacrifice performed by those persons that are conversant with
the rituals of sacrifices. It is He who rises every day in the firmament
(in the form of the sun) and divides Time into day and night, and courses
for half the year northwards and for half the year southwards.
Innumerable rays of light emanate from Him upwards and downwards and
transversely and illumine the earth. Brahmanas conversant with the Vedas
adore Him. Taking a portion of His rays the sun shines in the firmament.
Month after month, the sacrificer ordains Him as a sacrifice. Regenerate
persons conversant with the Vedas sing His praises in sacrifices of all
kinds. He it is that constitutes the wheel of the year, having three
naves and seven horses to drag it. It is in this way that He supports the
triple mansion (of the seasons). Endued with great energy, pervading all
things, the foremost of all creatures, it is Krishna who alone upholds
all the worlds. He is the sun, the dispeller of all darkness. He is the
Creator of all. Do thou, O hero, approach that Krishna! Once on a time,
the high-souled and puissant Krishna dwelt, for a while, in the form of
Agni in the forest of Khandava among some straw or dry grass. Soon was He
gratified (for he consumed all the medicinal herbs in that forest)."
}

created the earth and heaven and the space between. Indeed, it is this
Krishna of immeasurable and blazing energy who has created the forests

paralysed him. He is the one great Indra that is adored by the Brahmanas

Krishna, O king, who alone was able to keep the Rishi Durvasa of great

ancient Rishi. He is the Creator of the universe. Indeed, He creates
everything from His own nature. Superior to all the deities it is He who

Pradyumna, enraged by certain Brahmanas, came to me and said, 'O slayer
of Madhu, what merit attaches to the worship of the Brahmanas? Whence is
their lordship derived both here and hereafter? O giver of honours, what
rewards are won by constantly worshipping the Brahmanas? Do thou kindly
explain this clearly to me, for my mind is disturbed by doubts in respect
of this.' When these words were addressed to me by Pradyumna, I answered
him as follows. Do thou hear, O king, with close attention, what those
words were, 'O child of Rukmin, listen to me as I tell thee what the
prosperity is that one may win by worshipping the Brahmanas. When one
sets oneself to the acquisition of the well-known aggregate of three
(viz., Righteousness, Wealth, and Pleasure), or to the achievement of
Emancipation, or to that of fame and prosperity, or to the treatment and
cure of disease, or to the worship of the deities and the Pitris, one
should take care to gratify the regenerate ones. They are each a king
Soma (that sheds such agreeable light in the firmament.) They are
dispensers of happiness and misery. O child of Rukmini, whether in this
or in the next world, O son, everything agreeable has its origin in the
Brahmanas. I have no doubt in this! From the worship of the Brahmanas
flow mighty achievements and fame and strength. The denizens of all the
worlds, and the Regents of the universe, are all worshippers of
Brahmanas. How then, O son, can we disregard them, filled with the idea
that we are lords of the earth? O mighty-armed one, do not suffer thy
wrath to embrace the Brahmanas as its object. In this as also in the next
world, Brahmanas are regarded as beings. They have direct knowledge of
everything in the universe. Verily, they are capable of reducing
everything into ashes, if angry. They are capable of creating other
worlds and other Regents of worlds (than those that exist). Why then
should not persons who are possessed of energy and correct knowledge
behave with obedience and respect towards them? Formerly, in my house, O
son, dwelt the Brahmana Durvasa whose complexion was green and tawny.

long and he was exceedingly emaciated. He was taller in stature than the
tallest man on earth. Wandering over all the worlds, viz., that which

superior beings, even this was the verse which he sang constantly among
assemblies and in public squares. "Who is there that would cause the
Brahmana Durvasa to dwell in his house, doing the duties of hospitality
towards him? He becomes enraged with every one if he finds even the
slightest transgression. Hearing this regarding my disposition, who is
there that will give me refuge? Indeed, he that would give me shelter as
a guest should not do anything to anger me!" When I saw that no one
ventured to give him shelter in his house, I invited him and caused him
to take up his residence in my abode. On certain days he would eat the
food sufficient for the needs of thousands of persons. On certain other
days he would eat very little. On some days he would go out of my house
and would not return. He would sometimes laugh without any ostensible
reason and sometimes cry as causelessly. At that time there was nobody on
earth that was equal to him in years. One day, entering the quarters
assigned to him he burnt all the beds and coverlets and all the
well-adorned damsels that were there for serving him. Doing this, he went

  "passage_text": "SECTION CLXI\n\n\"'Vasudeva said, \"O mighty-armed Yudhishthira, listen to me as I recite to\nthee the many names of Rudra as also the high blessedness of that\nhigh-souled one. The Rishis describe Mahadeva as Agni, and Sthanu, and\nMaheswara; as one-eyed, and three-eyed, of universal form, and Siva or\nhighly auspicious. Brahmanas conversant with the Vedas say that that god\nhas two forms. One of these is terrible, and the other mild and\nauspicious. Those two forms, again, are subdivided into many forms. That\nform which is fierce and terrible is regarded as identical with Agni and\nLightning and Surya. The other form which is mild and auspicious is\nidentical with Righteousness and water and Chandramas. Then, again, it is\nsaid that half his body is fire and half is Soma (or the moon). That form\nof his which is mild and auspicious is said to be engaged in the practice\nof the Brahmacharya vow. The other form of his which is supremely\nterrible is engaged in all operations of destruction in the universe.\nBecause he is great (Mahat) and the Supreme Lord of all (Iswara),\ntherefore he is called Maheswara. And since he burns and oppresses, is\nkeen and fierce, and endued with great energy, and is engaged in eating\nflesh and blood and marrow, he is said to be Rudra. Since he is the\nforemost of all the deities, and since his dominion and acquisitions are\nvery extensive, and since he protects the extensive universe, therefore\nhe is called Mahadeva. Since he is of the form or colour of smoke,\ntherefore he is called Dhurjati. Since by all his acts he performs\nsacrifices for all and seeks the good of every creature, therefore he is\ncalled Siva or the auspicious one. Staying above (in the sky) he burns\nthe lives of all creatures and is, besides, fixed in a particular route\nfrom which he does not deviate. His emblem, again, is fixed and immovable\nfor all time. He is, for these reasons, called Sthanu. He is also of\nmultiform aspect. He is present, past, and future. He is mobile and\nimmobile. For this he is called Vahurupa (of multiform aspect). The\ndeities called Viswedevas reside in his body. He is, for this, called\nViswarupa (of universal form). He is thousand-eyed; or, he is\nmyriad-eyed; or, he has eyes on all sides and on every part of his body.\nHis energy issues through his eyes. There is no end of his eyes. Since he\nalways nourishes all creatures and sports also with them, and since he is\ntheir lord or master, therefore he is called Pasupati (the lord of all\ncreatures). Since his emblem is always observant of the vow of\nBrahmacharya, all the worlds worship it accordingly. This act of worship\nis said to gratify him highly. If there is one who worship him by\ncreating his image, another who worships his emblem, the latter it is\nthat attains to great prosperity for ever. The Rishis, the deities, the\nGandharvas, and the Apsaras, worship that emblem of his which is ever\nerect and upraised. If his emblem is worshipped, Maheswara becomes highly\ngratified with the worshipper. Affectionate towards his devotees, he\nbestows happiness upon them with a cheerful soul. This great god loves to\nreside in crematoria and there he burns and consumes all corpses. Those\npersons that perform sacrifices on such grounds attain at the end to\nthose regions which have been set apart for heroes. Employed in his\nlegitimate function, he it is that is regarded as the Death that resides\nin the bodies of all creatures. He is, again, those breaths called Prana\nand Apana in the bodies of all embodied beings. He has many blazing and\nterrible forms. All those forms are worshipped in the world and are known\nto Brahmanas possessed of knowledge. Amongst the gods he has many names\nall of which are fraught with grave import. Verily, the meanings of those\nnames are derived from either his greatness or vastness, or his feats, or\nhis conduct. The Brahmanas always recite the excellent Sata-rudriya in\nhis honour, that occurs in the Vedas as also that which has been composed\nby Vyasa. Verily, the Brahmanas and Rishis call him the eldest of all\nbeings. He is the first of all the deities, and it was from his mouth\nthat he created Agni. That righteous-souled deity, ever willing to grant\nprotection to all, never gives up his suppliants. He would much rather\nabandon his own life-breaths and incur all possible afflictions himself.\nLong life, health and freedom from disease, affluence, wealth, diverse\nkinds of pleasures and enjoyments, are conferred by him, and it is he\nalso who snatches them away. The lordship and affluence that one sees in\nSakra and the other deities are verily his. It is he who is always\nengaged in all that is good and evil in the three worlds. In consequence\nof his fullest control over all objects of enjoyment he is called Iswara\n(the Supreme Lord or Master). Since, again, he is the master of the vast\nuniverse, he is called Maheswara. The whole universe is pervaded by him\nin diverse forms. It is that deity whose mouth roars and burns the waters\nof the sea in the form of the huge mare's head!\"'\"[618]"

  "passage_text": "SECTION CLXII\n\n\"Vaisampayana said, 'After Krishna, the son of Devaki, had said these\nwords, Yudhishthira once more asked Bhishma the son of Santanu, saying,\n\"O thou of great intelligence, O foremost of all persons conversant with\nduties, which, indeed, of the two, direct perception and the scriptures,\nis to be regarded as authority for arriving at a conclusion?\"\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"I think, there is no doubt in this. Listen to me, O thou\nof great wisdom! I shall answer thee. The question thou hast asked is\ncertainly proper. It is easy to cherish doubt. But the solution of that\ndoubt is difficult. Innumerable are the instances, in respect of both\ndirect perception and audition (or the scriptures), in which doubts may\narise. Certain persons, who delight in the name of logicians, verily\nimagining themselves to be possessed of superior wisdom, affirm that\ndirect perception is the only authority. They assert that nothing,\nhowever true, is existent which is not directly perceivable; or, at least\nthey doubt the existence of those objects. Indeed, such assertions\ninvolve an absurdity and they who make them are of foolish understanding,\nwhatever may be their pride of learning. If, on the other hand, thou\ndoubtest as to how the one (indivisible Brahman) could be the cause, I\nanswer that one would understand it only after a long course of years and\nwith the assistance of Yoga practised without idleness. Indeed, O\nBharata, one that lives according to such means as present themselves\n(without, i.e., one's being wedded to this or that settled mode of life),\nand one that is devoted (to the solution of the question), would be\ncapable of understanding it. None else, truly, is competent for\ncomprehending it. When one attains to the very end of reasons (or\nreasoning processes), one then attains to that excellent and all\ncomprehending knowledge--that vast mass of effulgence which illumines all\nthe universe (called Brahma). That knowledge, O king, which is derived\nfrom reason (or inferences) can scarcely be said to be knowledge. Such\nknowledge should be rejected. It should be noted that it is not defined\nor comprehended by the word. It should, therefore, be rejected!\"[619]\n\n\"'Yudhisthira said, \"Tell me, O grandsire, which among these (four) is\nmost authoritative, viz., direct perception, inference from observation,\nthe science of Agama or scriptures, and diverse kinds of practices that\ndistinguish the good.\"\n\n\"'Bhishma said, \"While Righteousness is sought to be destroyed by wicked\npersons possessed of great might, it is capable of being protected for\nthe time being by those that are good exerting themselves with care and\nearnestness. Such protection, however, avails not in the long run, for\ndestruction does overtake Righteousness at the end. Then, again,\nRighteousness often proves a mask for covering Unrighteousness, like\ngrass and straw covering the mouth of a deep pit and concealing it from\nthe view. Hear, again, O Yudhisthira! In consequence of this, the\npractices of the good are interfered with and destroyed by the wicked.\nThose persons who are of evil conduct, who discard the Srutis--indeed,\nthose wicked wights who are haters of Righteousness,--destroy that good\ncourse of conduct (which could otherwise be set up as a standard). Hence,\ndoubts attach to direct perception, inference, and good conduct.[620]\nThose, therefore, among the good that are possessed of understanding born\nof (or cleansed by) the scriptures and that are ever contented, are to be\nregarded as the foremost. Let those that are anxious and deprived of\ntranquillity of soul, approach these. Indeed, O Yudhishthira, do thou\npay court to them and seek of them the solutions of thy doubt![621]\nDisregarding both pleasure and wealth which always follow cupidity and\nawakened into the belief that only Righteousness should be sought, do\nthou, O Yudhishthira, wait upon and ask those persons (for enlightening\nthyself). The conduct of those persons never goes wrong or meets with\ndestruction, as also their sacrifices and Vedic study and rites. Indeed,\nthese three, viz., conduct as consisting of overt acts, behaviour in\nrespect of (mental) purity, and the Vedas together constitute\nRighteousness.\"\n\n\"'Yudhishthira said, \"O grandsire, my understanding is once more stupefied\nby doubt. I am on this side the ocean, employed in searching after the\nmeans of crossing it. I do not, however, behold the other shore of the\nocean! If these three, viz., the Vedas, direct perception (or acts that\nare seen), and behaviour (or, mental purity) together constitute what is\nto be regarded as authority, it can be alleged that there is difference\nbetween them. Righteousness then becomes really of three kinds, although\nit is one and indivisible.\""
}

As regards\nUnrighteousness, it may be said that, even when of large proportions, it\nis incapable of even touching Righteousness which is always protected by\nTime and which shines like a blazing fire. These are the two results\nachieved by Righteousness, viz., the stainlessness of the soul and\nunsusceptibility of being touched by Unrighteousness. Verily,\nRighteousness is fraught with victory. Its effulgence is so great that it\nillumines the three worlds. A man of wisdom cannot catch hold of a sinful\nperson and forcibly cause him to become righteous. I shall\ntell thee particularly what the duties truly are of the four orders. So\nfar as their bodies are concerned, the individuals belonging to all the\nfour orders have the five primal elements for the constituent\ningredients. Indeed, in this respect, they are all of the same substance.\nFor all that, distinctions exist between them in respect of both\npractices relating to life or the world and the duties of righteousness.\nNotwithstanding these distinctions, sufficient liberty of action is left\nto them in consequence of which all individuals may attain to an equality\nof condition. The regions of felicity which represent the consequences or\nrewards of Righteousness are not eternal, for they are destined to come\nto an end. Righteousness, however, is eternal. When the cause is eternal,\nwhy is the effect not so?[629] The answer to this is as follows. Only\nthat Righteousness is eternal which is not promoted by the desire of\nfruit or reward. (That Righteous, however, which is prompted by the\ndesire of reward, is not eternal. Hence, the reward though undesired that\nattaches to the first kind of Righteousness, viz., attainment of identity\nwith Brahman, is eternal. The reward, however, that attaches to that\nRighteousness prompted by desire of fruit. Heaven is not eternal).[630]\nAll men are equal in respect of their physical organism. All of them,\nagain, are possessed of souls that are equal in respect of their nature.\nWhen dissolution comes, all else dissolve away. What remains is the\ninceptive will to achieve Righteousness.   "passage_text": "SECTION CLXVII

"Vaisampayana said, 'Then the royal son of Kunti, having duly honoured
the citizens and the inhabitants of the province, dismissed them to their
respective homes. The Pandava king then consoled these women, who had
lost their heroic husbands and sons in the battle, with abundant gift of
wealth. Having recovered his kingdom, Yudhishthira of great wisdom caused
himself to be duly installed on the throne. That foremost of men then
assured all his subjects by diverse acts of good will. That foremost of
righteous men then set himself to earn the substantial blessing of the
Brahmanas, of the foremost military officers, and the leading citizens.
The blessed monarch having passed fifty nights in the capital recollected
the time indicated by his grandsire as the hour of his departure from
this world. Accompanied by a number of priests he then set out of the
city named after the elephant, having seen that the sun ceasing to go
southwards had begun to proceed in his northward course. Yudhishthira the
son of Kunti took with him a large quantity of clarified butter and
floral garlands and scents and silken cloths and excellent sandalwood and
Aquilaria Agallocha and dark sloe wood, for cremating the body of
Bhishma. Diverse kinds of costly garlands and gems also were among those
stores. Placing Dhritarashtra ahead and queen Gandhari celebrated for her
virtues, and his own mother Kunti and all his brothers also, Yudhishthira
of great intelligence, accompanied by Krishna and Vidura of great wisdom,
as also by Yuyutsu and Yuyudhana, and by his other relatives and
followers forming a large train, proceeded, his praises hymned the while
by eulogists and bards. The sacrificial fires of Bhishma were also borne
in the procession. Thus accompanied, the king set out from his city like
a second chief of the deities. Soon he came upon the spot where the son
of Santanu was still lying on his bed of arrows. He beheld his grandsire
waited upon with reverence by Parasara's son Vyasa of great intelligence,
by Narada, O royal sage, by Devala and Asita, and also by the remnant of
unslain kings assembled from various parts of the country. Indeed, the
king saw that his high-souled grandsire, as he lay on his heroic bed, was
guarded on all sides by the warriors appointed for that duty. Alighting
from his car, King Yudhishthira with his brothers saluted his grandsire,
the chastiser of all foes. They also saluted the Rishis with the
island-born Vyasa at their head. They were saluted in return by them.
Accompanied by his priests each of whom resembled the grandsire Brahman
himself, as also by his brothers, Yudhishthira of unfading glory then
approached that spot whereon Bhishma lay on his bed of arrows surrounded
by these reverend Rishis. Then king Yudhishthira the just, at the head of
his brothers, addressed that foremost one of Kuru's race, viz., the son
of the River Ganga, as he lay on that bed of his, saying, "I am
Yudhishthira, O king! Salutations to thee, O son of the River Janhavi! If
thou hearest me still, tell me what I am to do for thee! Bearing with me
thy sacrificial fires, I have come here, O king, and wait upon thee at
the hour indicated! Preceptors of all branches of learning, Brahmanas,
Ritwiks, all my brothers, thy son, viz., king Dhritarashtra of great
energy, are all here with my counsellors as also Vasudeva of great
prowess. The remnant of unslain warriors, and all the denizens of
Kurujangala, are also here. Opening thy eyes, O chief of Kuru's race, do
thou behold them! Whatever should be done on this occasion has all been
arranged and provided for by me. Indeed, at this hour which thou hadst
indicated, all things have been kept ready!"

"Vaisampayana continued, 'Thus addressed by Kunti's son of great
intelligence, the son of Ganga opened his eyes and saw all the Bharatas
assembled there and standing around him. The mighty Bhishma then, taking
the strong hand of Yudhishthira, addressed him in a voice deep as that of
the clouds. That thorough master of words said, "By good luck, O son of
Kunti, thou hast come here with all thy counsellors, O Yudhishthira! The
thousand-rayed maker of day, the holy Surya has begun his northward
course. I have been lying on my bed here for eight and fifty nights.
Stretched on these sharp-pointed arrows I have felt this period to be as
long as if it was a century. O Yudhishthira, the lunar month of Magha has
come. This is, again, the lighted fortnight and a fourth part of it ought
by this (according to my calculations) be over." Having said so unto
Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, Ganga's son Bhishma then saluted
Dhritarashtra and said unto him as follows.'

"'Bhishma said, "O king, thou art well-conversant with duties. All thy
doubts, again, relating to the science of wealth have been well-solved.
Thou hast waited upon many Brahmanas of great learning. The subtle
sciences connected with the Vedas, all the duties of religion, O king,
and the whole of the four Vedas, are well-known to thee! Thou shouldst
not grieve, therefore, O son of Kuru! That which was pre-ordained has
happened. It could not be otherwise. Thou hast heard the mysteries
relating to the deities from the lips of the island-born Rishi himself.
Yudhishthira and his brothers are morally as much thy sons as they are
the sons of Pandu. Observant of the duties of religion, do thou cherish
and protect them. In their turn, they are always devoted to the service
of their seniors. King Yudhishthira the just is pure-souled. He will
always prove obedient to thee! I know that he is devoted to the virtue of
compassion or abstention from injury. He is devoted to his seniors and
preceptors. Thy sons were all wicked-souled. They were wedded to wrath
and cupidity. Overwhelmed by envy, they were all of wicked behavior. It
behoveth thee not to grieve for them!"'

"Vaisampayana continued, 'Having said this much unto Dhritarashtra of
great wisdom, the Kuru hero then addressed Vasudeva of mighty arms.'"
}

Thou art Vasudeva, thou art of golden body,\nthou art the one Purusha (or active agent), thou art the creator (of the\nuniverse), thou art of vast proportions. Thou art Jiva.
